front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah name is from the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The content of the Surah gives a strong clue that it occurred sometime after the Battle of the Trench (Shawwal, 5 A.H.). In Surah Al-Ahzab, Allah SWT briefly stated that an adopted son is not the same as a real son and that wives cannot become like mothers simply through a form of divorce such as zihār. But that Surah did not declare zihār a sin or specify its legal ruling. 

In contrast, Surah Al-Mujādilah provides detailed laws regarding this issue, which indicates that these Ayats were revealed later, offering a complete explanation of the matter that was only briefly mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Mujādilah teaches Muslims how to live by Allah SWT’s laws and maintain good manners in society. In the beginning, it warns believers not to follow old ignorant customs like zihār and reminds them that true faith means obeying Allah SWT completely. 

The Surah also teaches social manners — such as making space for others in gatherings, leaving politely when asked, and not disturbing the Prophet (PBUH) with unnecessary private talks. Finally, it explains that true believers are those who love Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH) more than anyone else, even their own families. Those who side with Allah SWT’s enemies are hypocrites, while sincere believers are the ones who belong to Allah’s group and will find success.

items.text: Main Themes of Surah Al-Mujādilah

Obeying Allah SWT’s Laws (1–6)
Muslims are told to follow Allah’s rules and not return to old ignorant customs like zihār (an unfair way of separating from one’s wife). Disobeying Allah SWT brings disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

Warning to Hypocrites (7–10)
The hypocrites secretly plotted against the Prophet (PBUH). Believers are told not to fear them and to speak only about good and righteous things when talking in private.

Good Manners in Gatherings (11–13)
Muslims are taught to make room for others in meetings, to leave politely when asked, and not to disturb the Prophet (PBUH) with unnecessary private talks. Those who want to speak to him privately should first give charity.

True Faith and Loyalty (14–22)
True believers love Allah SWT and His Messenger more than anyone else — even their families. Those who side with Allah’s enemies are hypocrites and belong to Satan’s group, while sincere believers are Allah’s true followers who will succeed.

sections.title: 1-6 PAGANS PRACTICE OF DIVORCE THROUGH 'ZIHAR' (CALLING HIS WIFE AS HIS MOTHER) IS PROHIBITED AND PENALTY FOR PRACTICING 'ZIHAR'

translation.text: Indeed, Allah has heard the argument of the woman who pleaded with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning her husband and appealed to Allah. Allah has heard your exchange. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

commentary.text: 3 times it is mentioned that Allah SWT heard and hears.
The reason for the revelation of Surah Al-Mujādilah (The Woman Who Pleads/Disputes) centers on a deeply moving incident involving Khawlah bint Tha‘labah and her husband Aws bin al-Sāmit.

Khawlah approached the Prophet (PBUH) in distress because her husband had pronounced ẓihār on her — an old pre-Islamic custom in which a man would say to his wife, “You are to me like my mother’s back,” intending to separate from her without giving her the rights of a proper divorce. This left women neither truly married nor free.

Khawlah pleaded with the Prophet (PBUH), explaining how her husband had taken her youth, her wealth, and how she had borne many children for him. Now that she was older and could no longer bear children, he had unjustly cast her aside. The Prophet (PBUH) could not do anything. She then cried out, “O Allah, I complain to You!”

While she was speaking, revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH), and Allah SWT revealed this Ayat thus affirming that Allah SWT Himself had heard her plea — a powerful reminder that no cry for justice goes unheard by Him.
Even ‘Aishah (RA), who was in another part of the room at the time, later expressed amazement, saying:

“All praise be to Allah, Who hears all voices. The woman came to the Prophet (PBUH)  arguing with him while I was in another part of the room and could not hear what she said — yet Allah , the Exalted, heard her from above the seven heavens.”

This incident moved the companions deeply. It not only abolished the cruel custom of ẓihār but also demonstrated Allah SWT’s closeness and compassion — that He listens to even the faintest plea of the oppressed.

translation.text: Those of you who ˹sinfully˺ divorce their wives by comparing them to their mothers ˹should know that˺ their wives are in no way their mothers. None can be their mothers except those who gave birth to them. What they say is certainly detestable and false. Yet Allah is truly Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.

commentary.text: The incident began when Khawlah bint Tha‘labah argued with her husband Aws bin al-Sāmit, who, in a moment of anger, said to her: “You are to me like the back of my mother.” This statement, known as Zihār, meant that the husband would treat his wife as unlawful to him, as one treats his own mother — yet without freeing her from the marriage bond. Soon after saying this, Aws regretted his words and attempted to resume relations, but Khawlah refused, saying that they must first seek guidance from Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH).

She went to the Prophet (PBUH), explained her situation, and pleaded her case, describing how her husband had taken her youth and strength, and now, in her older age, had wronged her. The Prophet (PBUH) initially advised her gently to be patient with her elderly husband, but while she was still speaking, revelation descended upon him. Allah revealed Ayat 1.

Allah SWT then clarified that when men make such statements, their wives do not become their mothers, for only those who gave birth to them are their true mothers. Calling one’s wife “like my mother” is a false and sinful statement, but Allah SWT, out of mercy, provided a means of forgiveness through atonement instead of making it a permanent separation.

Thus, these Ayats corrected a deep social wrong from pre-Islamic Arabia, showing Allah SWT’s justice, mercy, and concern for women’s rights, and honored Khawlah bint Tha‘labah as the woman whose plea was heard above the seven heavens.

translation.text: Those who divorce their wives in this manner, then ˹wish to˺ retract what they said, must free a slave before they touch each other. This ˹penalty˺ is meant to deter you. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

But if the husband cannot afford this, let him then fast two consecutive months before the couple touch each other. But if he is unable ˹to fast˺, then let him feed sixty poor people. This is to re-affirm your faith in Allah and His Messenger. These are the limits set by Allah. And the disbelievers will suffer a painful punishment.

commentary.text: Through these Ayats, Allah SWT abolished the cruel custom of Zihār and replaced it with a clear law and atonement (kaffārah). The Prophet (PBUH) instructed Aws to atone for his words:
Free a slave, if possible.
If not, fast for two consecutive months.
If unable to fast, feed sixty poor people.

When Khawlah explained that her husband was old and poor, the Prophet (PBUH) arranged to help them both — giving Aws dates to distribute in charity, and Khawlah herself volunteered to contribute. The Prophet (PBUH) praised her, saying she had done well and should continue to treat her husband kindly.

translation.text: Indeed, those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be debased, just like those before them. We have certainly sent down clear revelations. And the disbelievers will suffer a humiliating punishment.
On the Day Allah resurrects them all together, He will then inform them of what they have done. Allah has kept account of it all, while they have forgotten it. For Allah is a Witness over all things.

sections.title: 7-13 ETIQUETTES OF HOLDING A MEETING AND ORDER TO SPEND IN CHARITY BEFORE CONSULTING THE RASOOL IN PRIVATE

translation.text: Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? If three converse privately, He is their fourth. If five, He is their sixth. Whether fewer or more, He is with them wherever they may be. Then, on the Day of Judgment, He will inform them of what they have done. Surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

commentary.text: Believers are reminded that nothing in the universe escapes Allah’ SWTs knowledge. He is fully aware of everything in the heavens and on the earth. Even when a few people whisper secretly (NAJWA), thinking their words are hidden, Allah SWT is present with them. Whether they are three, five, fewer, or more — He knows every word, thought, and intention. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will make known to them everything they did, for His knowledge encompasses all things.

From Ayat 7 to 10, Allah SWT directly addresses the hypocrites in the Muslim community. Outwardly, they appeared to be part of the believers, but inwardly, they formed a separate group that schemed and whispered among themselves. They held secret meetings to spread doubts, sow division, and weaken the unity of Muslims.
This Ayat exposes their behavior and serves as a warning: no secret plotting can ever escape Allah’s awareness.

When Allah SWT says He is the “fourth” among three or the “sixth” among five, it doesn’t mean He is physically present — rather, it emphasizes that His knowledge, power, and hearing are always present. He knows every hidden conversation and secret plan. The use of the numbers three and five adds rhythm and beauty to the verse, while the phrase “whether fewer or more” covers all other cases.

In essence, this Ayat teaches that Allah SWT’s presence is not limited by space or number — it is through His all-encompassing knowledge and awareness. Humans may hide their words from others, but not from Him. It’s both a warning to wrongdoers and a comfort to the sincere — reminding us that Allah SWT sees every injustice and hears every whisper, whether in the light or in the dark.

translation.text: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret talks, yet they ˹always˺ return to what they were forbidden from, conspiring in sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you ˹O Prophet˺, they greet you not as Allah greets you, and say to one another, “Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?” Hell is enough for them—they will burn in it. And what an evil destination!

commentary.text: Here is described the evil behavior of some Jews in Madinah who secretly conspired against the Prophet (PBUH) and mocked him through deceitful words. Although the Prophet (PBUH) had a peace agreement with them, they continued to whisper among themselves whenever a Muslim passed by, causing fear and suspicion.

Allah SWT revealed that their secret conversations (NAJWA) were only about sin, hostility, and disobedience to the Messenger. They would even greet the Prophet with twisted words, saying “As-sām ʿalayka” (death be upon you) instead of “As-salāmu ʿalayka” (peace be upon you). When ʿĀ’ishah (RA) angrily responded to them, the Prophet (PBUH) calmly told her that Allah SWT does not like rudeness and instructed her simply to reply “Wa ʿalaykum” (and upon you).

These people mocked the Prophet and thought that if he were truly sent by Allah SWT, they would be punished immediately for their words. In reply, Allah SWT declared that Hell would be enough for them as their final punishment. This passage exposes their hypocrisy and teaches Muslims to stay away from secret plotting, mockery, and foul speech, reminding them instead to speak only what is good and pleasing to Allah SWT.

translation.text: O believers! When you converse privately, let it not be for sin, aggression, or disobedience to the Messenger, but let it be for goodness and righteousness. And fear Allah, to Whom you will ˹all˺ be gathered.

commentary.text: NAJWĀ (secret conversation) is not forbidden in itself; its ruling depends on intention and purpose. If sincere people speak privately for good reasons — to resolve disputes, defend rights, or promote good — it is permissible and even praiseworthy. But if it involves sin, deceit, or plotting harm, it becomes sinful.

The Prophet (PBUH) taught that when three people are together, two should not whisper privately, as this causes the third distress. This also applies to speaking in an unknown language or making gestures that exclude others. Islam thus encourages openness, respect, and consideration in all communication.

translation.text: Secret talks are only inspired by Satan to grieve the believers. Yet he cannot harm them whatsoever except by Allah’s Will. So in Allah let the believers put their trust.

commentary.text: This Ayat teaches that if a believer sees others whispering and feels suspicious or hurt, they should not jump to conclusions or react with anger or malice. A true Muslim knows that no one can harm them except by Allah SWT’s will, and this trust protects them from unnecessary fear or resentment. Such faith brings peace of mind, allowing the believer to focus on good deeds instead of worrying about others’ schemes. A person who trusts Allah SWT is neither weak nor easily shaken by doubts, nor so small-minded as to respond to evil with injustice.

translation.text: O believers! When you are told to make room in gatherings, then do so. Allah will make room for you ˹in His grace˺. And if you are told to rise, then do so. Allah will elevate those of you who are faithful, and ˹raise˺ those gifted with knowledge in rank. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: After the topic of Najwa or secret discussions/conversations, Muslims are taught important lessons in manners, humility, and respect for others. When believers are told to make room for others in a gathering, they should do so willingly, for in return Allah SWT promises to grant them ease, honor, and blessing. This instruction applies not only to the Prophet’s (PBUH) gatherings but within all Muslim assemblies. It encourages courtesy, cooperation, and generosity of spirit.

The second part of the Ayat was revealed because some people would prolong their stay in the Prophet’s gatherings, causing him inconvenience. Allah SWT reminded them that true honor lies not in sitting close to the Prophet or remaining longest in his presence, but in faith and knowledge, which raise a person’s rank in Allah’s sight.

translation.text: O believers! When you consult the Messenger privately, give something in charity before your consultation. That is better and purer for you. But if you lack the means, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed to address the issue of people seeking private meetings with the Prophet (PBUH) too often and without real need, which caused him difficulty. According to Ibn Abbas, Muslims frequently requested private counsel, and though the Prophet (PBUH) never refused anyone, this became burdensome. At times, such private talks led to misunderstandings and rumors — people assumed secret discussions meant important political or military news, giving hypocrites a chance to mock the Prophet (PBUH) as being too trusting.

To prevent this misuse and protect the Prophet (PBUH)’s time, Allah SWT commanded that anyone wishing to speak privately with him must first give something in charity. This rule ensured that only those with sincere and important matters would approach him. Qatadah noted that some people had sought private meetings merely to display their status.

Ali (RA) narrated that when the Ayat was revealed, there was discussion as to how much charity should be given. Ali suggested small amounts, saying even half a dinar was too much for most people. Finally, a very small amount was set. Ali said, “This is a Ayat of the Quran which no one acted upon except me — I gave charity and then spoke privately with the Prophet (PBUH).” Hypocrites were too stingy and thus did not do private conversations after this.
FYI – This was abrogated soon after as noted in the next Ayat.

translation.text: Are you afraid of spending in charity before your private consultations ˹with him˺? Since you are unable to do so, and Allah has turned to you in mercy, then ˹continue to˺ establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: This second command was sent down some time after the first command, and it concealed the injunction of giving something in charity. However, there is a difference of opinion as to how long the injunction remained in force. Qatadah says it remained in force for less than a day and then was abrogated. Muqatil bin Hayyan says that it remained in force for ten days; and this is the longest period of its life mentioned in any tradition.
This proved who was sincere and who was a hypocrite.
And continue to observe Allah SWT’s commands.

sections.title: 14-22 THOSE WHO BEFRIEND THOSE WHO ARE UNDER THE WRATH OF ALLAH WILL BE SEVERELY PUNISHED AND TRUE BELIEVERS DO NOT BEFRIEND THOSE WHO OPPOSE ALLAH AND HIS RASOOL

translation.text: Have you not seen those ˹hypocrites˺ who ally themselves with a people with whom Allah is displeased? They are neither with you nor with them. And they swear to lies knowingly.

commentary.text: Allah SWT chastises the hypocrites, specifically the Jews, for secretly aiding and supporting the disbelievers even though, they were neither with the disbelievers nor with the Muslims.

When the hypocrites met the believers, they said that they believed and when they went to the Messenger, they swore to him by Allah SWT that they were believers. They knew that they were lying in their vow, and they knew that they did not declare their true creed. This is why Allah SWT witnessed here that they lie in their vows.

translation.text: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, it was evil that they were doing.
They have made their ˹false˺ oaths as a shield, hindering ˹others˺ from the cause of Allah. So they will suffer a humiliating punishment.

commentary.text: On the one hand, the hypocrites swear oaths to their faith and fidelity to make the Muslims believe that they belong to them, and on the other, they sow doubts and suspicions in the hearts of people against Islam and the Prophet (PBUH) so that they should turn away from Islam.
As recompense for belittling the significance of swearing by the Mighty Name of Allah, while lying and concealing betrayal they shall suffer a humiliating punishment.

translation.text: Neither their wealth nor children will be of any help to them against Allah whatsoever. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever.

commentary.text: None of their possessions can avert the affliction. They will be the dwellers of the Fire to dwell therein forever.

translation.text: On the Day Allah resurrects them all, they will ˹falsely˺ swear to Him as they swear to you, thinking they have something to stand on. Indeed, it is they who are the ˹total˺ liars.

commentary.text: Liars in this world will continue lying in the next even when they are in front of their Raab – who Knows, Hears and Sees All.

translation.text: Satan has taken hold of them, causing them to forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan. Surely Satan’s party is bound to lose

commentary.text: Shaytan has taken over their hearts to the point that he made them forget Allah SWT. This is what the devil does to those whom he controls.

translation.text: Indeed, the ones who oppose Allah and His Messenger - those will be among the most humbled.
Allah has decreed, “I and My messengers will certainly prevail.” Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

You will never find a people who ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and the Last Day loyal to those who defy Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their parents, children, siblings, or extended family. For those ˹believers˺, Allah has instilled faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. He will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. They are the party of Allah. Indeed, Allah’s party is bound to succeed.

commentary.text: Surah Taubah 24
This is the litmus test:
This Ayat declares a clear moral and spiritual principle: true faith and love for the enemies of Allah SWT cannot coexist in the same heart.

A believer’s loyalty and affection must lie firmly with Allah, His Messenger (PBUH), and His religion. If a person claims to believe in Islam but still maintains affectionate ties with those who oppose it, that claim is hollow. Faith demands sincerity and decisiveness — one cannot ride in two boats at once. Those who prefer their worldly relationships or social ties over their commitment to Islam are, in truth, showing hypocrisy rather than faith.

To illustrate this principle, Allah SWT points to the example of the early Muslims, whose loyalty to faith was proven through their actions. During the battles of Badr and Uhud, believers fought even against their closest relatives solely for the sake of Allah SWT. Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah killed his father, Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umair fought against his brother, and ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab killed his maternal uncle. Abu Bakr was prepared to face his son in battle, and ‘Ali, Hamzah, and ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Harith fought their own kin from Quraysh. These acts were not out of personal hatred but out of unwavering commitment to Allah and His Messenger. Their example showed that faith takes precedence over all other bonds — family, tribe, or friendship.

This Ayat thus defines the essence of true belief — loyalty to Allah SWT and His cause above all else. It calls on Muslims to purify their hearts from divided loyalties, to love for the sake of Allah SWT, and to stand firm in faith even when it requires sacrifice.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah derives its name from Ayat 2.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah Al-Hashr—also called Surah an-Nadir—was revealed entirely in connection with the expulsion of the Jewish tribe Banu an-Nadir from Madinah, shortly after their failed plot to assassinate the Prophet (PBUH) thus marking an important turning point in early Islamic governance and relations with the People of the Book.

items.text: After the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrated to Madinah, he formed a treaty of peace and mutual defense with the Jewish tribes living there — mainly Banu Qaynuqaʿ, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah.

These tribes had settled in Hejaz centuries earlier after being expelled from Palestine and Syria by the Romans. They had become Arab in language and culture but kept their Jewish religion and exclusivity.
Economically powerful, they controlled trade, crafts, and money lending, often exploiting Arab tribes through debt and high interest.
When Islam united the Arabs and forbade interest, the Jews viewed it as a threat to their influence and wealth.
Breakdown of Relations:
Banu Qaynuqaʿ were the first to violate the treaty after the Battle of Badr. They harassed Muslim women and provoked violence, leading to their expulsion from Madinah.
Banu Nadir then plotted to assassinate the Prophet (PBUH) under the guise of cooperation. Their plot was exposed, and they were ordered to leave Madinah.
Encouraged by Abdullah bin Ubayy (leader of the hypocrites), they refused.
The Prophet (PBUH) besieged them; they surrendered and were exiled, taking only what they could carry.
This event became the occasion of revelation for Surah Al-Hashr.

Divine Power and Justice:
The downfall of Banu Nadir was not due to Muslim might but Allah SWT’s decree — those who oppose Him are always defeated.

Ethics of Warfare:
Destruction for legitimate military purposes (e.g., cutting palm trees) is not “spreading mischief.”

Distribution of War Gains without battle (Fay):
The Surah sets rules for handling properties gained without battle — to benefit the Prophet (PBUH) , the poor, orphans, migrants, and society at large — preventing concentration of wealth among the rich.

Hypocrisy Exposed:
The hypocrites (munafiqeen) are rebuked for deceiving the Jews with false promises of help and betraying the Muslim community.
Moral and Spiritual Lessons: Believers are urged to:
Fear Allah and prepare for the Hereafter,
Reflect on the Quran,
Understand the difference between righteousness and sin,
Recognize Allah’s attributes of power, wisdom, and knowledge.

sections.title: 1-5 JEWISH TRIBE OF BANU AL-NADIR ARE GIVEN THE ORDER OF EXILE FOR THEIR MUTINY AGAINST THE ISLAMIC STATE

translation.text: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. For He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

He is the One Who expelled the disbelievers of the People of the Book from their homes for ˹their˺ first banishment ˹ever˺. You never thought they would go. And they thought their strongholds would put them out of Allah’s reach. But ˹the decree of˺ Allah came upon them from where they never expected. And He cast horror into their hearts so they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take a lesson ˹from this˺, O people of insight!

commentary.text: The Story Behind Surah Al-Hashr (Banu An-Nadir)
When the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) moved to Madinah, he made a peace agreement with the Jewish tribes, including Banu An-Nadir — that they would not fight each other or help anyone against the other.

After some time, the Prophet (PBUH) went to them to ask for help paying blood money (compensation) for two men who had been killed by mistake. They agreed outwardly — but secretly planned to drop a stone on the Prophet (PBUH) to kill him. Allah SWT informed His Prophet (PBUH) of their plot, and who immediately left the area safely.

When their treachery became known, the Prophet (PBUH) told them to leave Madinah within ten days or be ready for war. They refused, thinking their strong forts and wealth would protect them. But Allah SWT filled their hearts with fear, and after only a short siege of six days, they surrendered.
The Prophet (PBUH) allowed them to leave peacefully and take what their camels could carry, except weapons.
They destroyed their own houses by removing doors, beams, and wood so as to carry it with them.
Some of them went to Khaybar, others to Syria (Ash-Sham).

Their fertile lands and date gardens near Madinah were left behind and given by Allah to the Prophet (PBUH) as fay’(booty without battle). The Prophet distributed it mostly among the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and gave shares to only two poor men from the Ansar.
Lesson: Allah SWT blessed this Jewish tribe with so much, but they used they recourses to oppose Allah. Beware. They rejected, they opposed and were hypocrites.

translation.text: Had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have certainly punished them in this world. And in the Hereafter they will suffer the punishment of the Fire.

commentary.text: Had they fought instead of surrendering to save their lives, they would have been completely wiped out.

translation.text: Whatever palm trees you ˹believers˺ cut down or left standing intact, it was ˹all˺ by Allah’s Will, so that He might disgrace the rebellious.

commentary.text: During the siege of the Jewish tribe Banu an-Nadir, some of their date-palm trees were cut down or burned by the Muslims to clear the battlefield and weaken the enemy’s defense. The hypocrites and Jews objected, accusing the Prophet (PBUH) of causing corruption on earth, since Islam forbids needless destruction.

In response, Allah SWT revealed this Ayat affirming that whatever trees the Muslims cut or left standing was done by His permission, not as corruption but as a legitimate military necessity. This reassurance cleared the Muslims of any guilt and established that measured destruction in war, when required for strategy or safety, is lawful, while wanton ruin remains forbidden.

sections.title: 6-10 DISTRIBUTION OF THE BELONGINGS OF BANU AL-NADIR AND GOOD QUALITIES OF TRUE IMMIGRANTS AND GOOD QUALITIES OF TRUE ANSAR (THE RESIDENTS OF MADINAH)

translation.text: As for the gains Allah has turned over to His Messenger from them—you did not ˹even˺ spur on any horse or camel for such gains. But Allah gives authority to His messengers over whoever He wills. For Allah is Most Capable of everything.

commentary.text: Also see Surah Anfal

The Fai' and how it is spent
Allah SWT explains the regulations for Fai', the booty that the Muslims acquire from the disbelievers, without fighting them or using cavalry and camelry in war against them.
For instance, the booty collected from Bani An-Nadir was not acquired because of fighting them using horses and camels. The Muslims did not fight Bani An-Nadir in battle, but Allah SWT forced them out of their forts on account of the fear that He placed in their hearts. Therefore, it was Fai' that Allah SWT awarded His Messenger, with his discretion to spend it however he sees fit.

translation.text: As for gains granted by Allah to His Messenger from the people of ˹other˺ lands, they are for Allah and the Messenger, his close relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travellers so that wealth may not merely circulate among your rich. Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it. And whatever he forbids you from, leave it. And fear Allah. Surely Allah is severe in punishment.

commentary.text: This Ayat lays down who receives the property (faiʾ) after Banu An-Nadir’s exile: it belongs ultimately to Allah SWT, and is to be used for the Messenger, his kin (Banu Hashim/Banu al-Muttalib), orphans, the needy, and wayfarers, so that wealth does not remain trapped only among the rich.

Historically the Prophet (PBUH) used a portion for his household and for equipping the community, and after him the caliphs treated those shares as public revenue for collective welfare. All agree the aim is redistribution and social justice (complementing zakat) rather than private enrichment.

This ensures circulation of wealth and equity. That is, only one group is not getting richer. There are balance and equality in society.  Fakar (poverty) leads to kufur at times as one class is living a debouched, decadent and extravagant lifestyle while the other is barely making ends meet working day and night.

The Ayat therefore establishes both an economic principle—state revenues should circulate to relieve poverty—and a legal rule distinguishing faiʾ (state-held property not captured in battle) from ghanimah (spoils shareable among fighters). Finally, it commands obedience to the Prophet (PBUH)’s decisions about such matters and warns believers to fear Allah SWT, since divine authority and accountability underlie the whole arrangement.

translation.text: ˹Some of the gains will be˺ for poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes and wealth, seeking Allah’s bounty and pleasure, and standing up for Allah and His Messenger. They are the ones true in faith.

commentary.text: This means the Muhajir—those who were forced to leave Makkah and other places because they became Muslims—have a rightful share in the fai. Before the Banu An-Nadir settlement was taken, these emigrants had no stable livelihood, so the Prophet (PBUH) used part of that property to support them (and the Ansar’s reserved oases were returned).

More broadly, the Ayat establishes a lasting duty: the Islamic community (using fai and zakat) must economically settle and support people who are compelled to emigrate for the sake of God and His Messenger, helping them regain self-sufficiency until the Day of Resurrection.

translation.text: As for those who had settled in the city and ˹embraced˺ the faith before ˹the arrival of˺ the emigrants, they love whoever immigrates to them, never having a desire in their hearts for whatever ˹of the gains˺ is given to the emigrants. They give ˹the emigrants˺ preference over themselves even though they may be in need. And whoever is saved from the selfishness of their own souls, it is they who are ˹truly˺ successful.

commentary.text: A second group is now being mentioned. Allah SWT is praising the Ansâr — the Madīnan Muslims who welcomed the Muhājirīn — and summarizes their selfless spirit: they owned the city and embraced Islam before the emigrants arrived, they loved and cared for the newcomers, shared their gardens and resources without envy, and often preferred the emigrants’ needs above their own despite hardship. The Prophet (PBUH) and early sources record numerous examples: the Ansâr offered their date-palms and produce, sheltered and fed guests while going hungry themselves, and accepted the emigrants as partners and brothers.

This Ayat contrasts this largeness of heart with shuhha (stinginess or narrow-mindedness), warning that greed destroys communities. In short: the Ansâr are held as a model of generosity and communal solidarity, and it teaches that overcoming selfishness is both a moral excellence and a path to true prosperity.

translation.text: And those who come after them will pray, “Our Lord! Forgive us and our fellow believers who preceded us in faith, and do not allow bitterness into our hearts towards those who believe. Our Lord! Indeed, You are Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.”

commentary.text: This Ayat extends the entitlement to faiʾ (publicly held spoils/lands) to later generations — not just the emigrants (Muhājirūn) and the Helpers (Ansār) — and teaches believers to pray for earlier Muslims: “Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith; remove rancour from our hearts toward the believers; You are Most Merciful.”

Practically, this clause underpinned ʿUmar’s policy to treat conquered lands as communal revenue for present and future Muslims rather than parcel them out permanently to conquerors. Morally, it commands unity and goodwill across generations of Muslims: do not harbor malice and pray for the forgiveness of those who came before. Jurists used the Ayat to justify long-term public stewardship of territory (jizyah/revenue systems) and to caution against greed, partisanship, and retrospective vilification of earlier companions — virtues central to communal stability and justice.
Collective ownership of land.

Identifies the third group entitled to fai—those who followed the Muhājirīn and Anṣār in faith—and records their prayer asking Allah SWT to forgive earlier believers and remove hatred from their hearts, teaching unity and intergenerational solidarity.

sections.title: 11-17 HYPOCRITES CONSPIRACY WITH THE PEOPLE OF THE BOOK AND PARABLE OF A SHAITAN VS A DISBELIEVER

translation.text: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen the hypocrites who say to their fellow disbelievers from the People of the Book, “If you are expelled, we will certainly leave with you, and We will never obey anyone against you. And if you are fought against, we will surely help you.”? But Allah bears witness that they are truly liars.

commentary.text: Now the opposite is being mentioned. When the Prophet (PBUH) ordered Banu an-Nadir to leave Madīnah the hypocrites — led by ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy — promised the Jews military aid and encouraged them to stand firm. Allah SWT therefore revealed the passage to expose and rebuke hypocrisy, false promises, and conspiracies before the siege. Allah SWT bears witness that the hypocrites are lying an in fact they never helped the Jews.

Historically the passage is an earlier revelation than the Ayats about the tribe’s actual expulsion, but in the Qurān the two passages are placed with the later (expulsion) material first because its subject-matter is considered of greater immediate importance.

translation.text: Indeed, if they are expelled, the hypocrites will never leave with them. And if they are fought against, the hypocrites will never help them. And even if the hypocrites did so, they would certainly flee, then the disbelievers would be left with no help.

commentary.text: Allah SWT reveals the hypocrisy that is lip service only with no follow up. The hypocrites will not fight along with the Jews nor did they help.

translation.text: Even united, they would not ˹dare˺ fight against you except ˹from˺ within fortified strongholds or from behind walls. Their malice for each other is intense: you think they are united, yet their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people with no ˹real˺ understanding.

commentary.text: The hypocrites’ second fundamental weakness: besides cowardice, they lacked any real, positive bond—only mutual hypocrisy and jealous ambition united them. Their cooperation was negative (opposed to Muhammad’s leadership) rather than constructive; each leader guarded his own faction and resented the others.

Because their unity rested on envy and self-interest, their loud threats of joining the Jews and other tribes were empty bluster and would quickly evaporate when tested. The practical point: the Muslims need not be unduly alarmed by the hypocrites’ boasting, for it masks internal weakness, not real strength.
Hypocrisy produces brittle alliances!

translation.text: ˹They are˺ like Satan when he lures someone to disbelieve. Then after they have done so, he will say ˹on Judgment Day˺, “I have absolutely nothing to do with you. I truly fear Allah—the Lord of all worlds.”

commentary.text: That is, these hypocrites are treating the Bani an-Nadir in much the same way as Satan treats men. Today they are urging them to stand firm and go forth and clash with the Muslims making them believe that they would come to their aid, but when they clash with the Muslims, they would renounce their pledges and promises.

Also see Surah al-Anfal, Ayat 48. The same way does Satan treat every disbeliever. First, he incited them with false hopes and brought them out to confront the Muslims, saying: Today no one can overcome you, for I am with you. But when the two forces met in battle, he took to his heels, saying: I have nothing to do with you. I see that which you cannot see. Indeed, I fear Allah.

The example of the Jews being deceived by the promises of the hypocrites, who said that they will help them if Muslims fight them, is that of the devil. When matters got serious and the Jews were besieged, the hypocrites betrayed them and abandoned them to taste utter defeat. Likewise, the devil lures mankind into disbelief and when they obey him, he disowns them and declares himself free of their actions, saying,

sections.title: 18-20 LET EACH SOUL SEE WHAT IT IS SENDING FOR THE HEREAFTER

translation.text: O believers! Be mindful of Allah and let every soul look to what ˹deeds˺ it has sent forth for tomorrow. And fear Allah, ˹for˺ certainly Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: IMAN (TAQWA) + GOOD DEEDS= SUCCESS

This passage teaches a compact, powerful lesson: the Prophet (PBUH) called people to taqwā (God-consciousness) and to prepare for the Day of Reckoning by measuring what they send ahead (good deeds, charity, summons to right conduct).
Fear Allah SWT Who is always watching and aware of what we do and think about what you are sending ahead.

Hadith: A man had three friends (i) One said take from me whatever you want (Wealth) (ii) Second said I am with you but will leave you at the time of death (Family) (iii) I am with you in life and death. (Good deeds)

translation.text: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. It is they who are ˹truly˺ rebellious.

commentary.text: Remembering God keeps a person anchored to right conduct; losing that remembrance makes them liable to stray into sinful behavior. Prepare for the meeting with Allah SWT on the DoJ.

Lesson: For us to achieve our higher self and not behave like animals we must not forget our Creator. So that this vessel we are given is used in the right purpose. Allama Iqbal’s philosophy of Khudi (Selfhood) was derived from this Ayat.

commentary.text: The people of Hell and Paradise are not the same. People of Paradise are the successful ones.

sections.title: 21 AL-QURAN COULD EVEN AFFECT A MOUNTAIN

translation.text: Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain, you would have certainly seen it humbled and torn apart in awe of Allah. We set forth such comparisons for people, ˹so˺ perhaps they may reflect.

commentary.text: Allah SWT emphasizes the greatness of the Quran, its high status; worthy of making hearts humble.

The parable says that if its message were placed on a mountain the mountain would humble itself and split from awe, so what about human hearts — which can understand the Book — be moved to humility, reflection and obedience.

A mighty mountain is humbled and would tremble with fear. Yet many people—who hear and understand the Quran and know they will answer to God—remain unmoved and careless, behaving as if they were lifeless stones.

Parables and Prophetic reports (the weeping tree trunk, mountains that would shatter or give forth water) are cited to show the Quran’s power to stir even the inanimate, and therefore to shame spiritual dullness in people who hear it without being shaken.

THE POINT: Genuine faith produces awe, self-examination, and moral urgency. Hearing the Quranic message without being shaken by it is a sign of spiritual heedlessness. Manners, actions, thoughts all change after reading and reflecting upon the Quran.
Lesson: Quran nay mera kuch nahi bigara.

sections.title: 22-24 FIFTEEN EXCLUSIVE ATTRIBUTES OF ALLAH

arabic_lines: هُوَ اللّٰهُ الَّذِىۡ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَ ۚ عٰلِمُ الۡغَيۡبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ ۚ هُوَ الرَّحۡمٰنُ الرَّحِيۡمُ

translation.text: He is Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him: Knower of the seen and unseen. He is the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: اللَّهُ — Allāh — (God)
العَلِيمُ — Al-ʿAlīm — (All-Knowing)
الرَّحْمَـٰنُ — Ar-Raḥmān — (Most-Merciful)
الرَّحِيمُ — Ar-Raḥīm — (Most-Compassionate)
Key points:
God is singular and supreme (no rival).
God is omniscient (knows everything, without need of means).
God’s mercy is universal and unique.

The attributes are given to awaken awe, accountability, and correct self-understanding. They stress His uniqueness (no partner or rival), His perfect, direct knowledge of past, present and future (nothing is hidden from Him), and His vast, encompassing mercy that sustains creation.

Placing these divine attributes immediately after the warning about heedlessness and the Quran’s stirring power is deliberate: it transforms legal and moral commands into a solemn personal responsibility, reminding people that they answer to an all-powerful, all-knowing, supremely merciful Being (the commentary links this sweep of attributes with the comprehensive portraits found in Áyatul-Kursî and nearby passages).

arabic_lines: هُوَ اللّٰهُ الَّذِىۡ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَۚ اَلۡمَلِكُ الۡقُدُّوۡسُ السَّلٰمُ الۡمُؤۡمِنُ الۡمُهَيۡمِنُ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡجَـبَّارُ الۡمُتَكَبِّرُؕ سُبۡحٰنَ اللّٰهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُوۡنَ

commentary.text: This Ayat lists a cluster of divine Names and attributes below: Placing these attributes here (after warnings about heedlessness and the Quran’s power) is meant to awaken humility, trust, accountability and correct worship: we answer to a Sovereign who is pure, powerful, and wholly transcendent, so associating partners with Him is incoherent and unjustified.

ٱلْقُدُّوسُ — Al-Quddūs — (The Holy / Pure/, free of flaw or defect.

God’s Names here demand awe, trust, and exclusive devotion — He is the unique, pure, powerful Sovereign before whom we will be held accountable.

arabic_lines: هُوَ اللّٰهُ الۡخَـالِـقُ الۡبَارِئُ الۡمُصَوِّرُ لَـهُ الۡاَسۡمَآءُ الۡحُسۡنٰىؕ يُسَبِّحُ لَهٗ مَا فِى السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡحَكِيۡمُ

translation.text: He is Allah: the Creator, the Inventor, the Shaper. He ˹alone˺ has the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Him. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is the ultimate Planner (Creator), Executor (Originator) and Fashioner (Shaper) of everything — He conceives the design, brings things into existence, and gives them their final form.

The Ayat affirms that all the most beautiful names and attributes belong to Him alone, and that everything in the heavens and earth praises His glory. It closes by reminding us of His supreme power and wisdom: He alone ordains the universe with purpose and perfection, so worship and trust are due to Him alone.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The name of this Surah “Al-Mumtahinah” is from Ayat 10.

Al-Mumtahinah (الممتحنة) — “The Surah which examines.”

Al-Mumtahanah (الممتحنة) — “The woman who is examined.”

Thus, the name reflects the testing or examination of the faith of emigrating women who sought refuge in the Muslim community.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The Surah was revealed between the Truce of Ḥudaibiyyah (6 A.H.) and the Conquest of Makkah (8 A.H.).

This timing is confirmed by three historically known incidents:

items.text: The Case of Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah:

Before the conquest of Makkah, Ḥāṭib secretly sent a letter to the Quraysh chiefs revealing the Prophet’s (PBUH) war plans. Allah SWT exposed this act, and the Surah’s opening Ayats address this event, warning against divided loyalties.
The Issue of Emigrant Women:

After the Treaty of Ḥudaibiyyah, Muslim women began migrating from Makkah to Madinah, while their non-Muslim husbands remained behind. The question arose: Should these women be returned under the terms of the truce, or accepted as Muslims?
Allah SWT revealed guidance declaring that believing women were not to be returned to the disbelievers, as their marriage bonds were nullified.
The pledge (bayʿah) that women were to take upon embracing Islam — a practice that became significant when many Quraysh women accepted Islam soon after the Conquest of Makkah.
1. Loyalty and Alliance (Ayats 1–9 & 13)
Theme: Prohibition of secret alliances with enemies of Islam.
Refers to the incident of Ḥātib ibn Abī Balta‘ah, a Companion who sent a secret message to Quraysh before the conquest of Makkah to protect his family.

Lesson: Believers must never aid or ally with that hostile to Islam, even for personal motives. However, kindness and justice are allowed towards non-Muslims who are not hostile or persecuting believers.
Moral Principle: Faith and active friendship with enemies of the faith cannot coexist.
2. Legal and Social Rulings (Ayat 10–11)
Theme: Marital bonds between Muslim and non-Muslim spouses.
Context: After Hijrah, some Muslim women migrated from Makkah leaving their pagan husbands, and some Muslim men in Madinah had wives who remained unbelievers.
Ruling: A Muslim woman cannot remain married to a non-Muslim man, and vice versa.
Significance: Establishes clear legal principles for Muslim family law. Protects the moral and religious integrity of the Muslim household.
3. Women’s Pledge and Moral Reform (Ayat 12)
Theme: Moral reformation and social purification.
Instruction: The Prophet (PBUH) was commanded to take a pledge (Bay‘ah) from women who embraced Islam, promising to abstain from:
Shirk (idolatry)
Theft
Adultery
Killing their children
Slander
Disobedience in good matters
Purpose: To instill a sense of moral discipline and accountability. To reform pre-Islamic customs and elevate women’s ethical role in society.
Outcome: Marks the integration of new believers into the Islamic moral and social system.

sections.title: 1-3 DO NOT BE FRIEND WITH THOSE WHO ARE ENEMIES OF ALLAH AND THE MUSLIMS

translation.text: O believers! Do not take My enemies and yours as trusted allies, showing them affection even though they deny what has come to you of the truth. They drove the Messenger and yourselves out ˹of Mecca˺, simply for your belief in Allah, your Lord. If you ˹truly˺ emigrated to struggle in My cause and seek My pleasure, ˹then do not take them as allies,˺ disclosing secrets ˹of the believers˺ to the pagans out of affection for them, when I know best whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal. And whoever of you does this has truly strayed from the Right Way.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 13
The first Ayats of Surah Al-Mumtahanah were revealed about a Companion Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah shortly before the Conquest of Makkah.

Although he was a sincere believer and one of those who had fought at Badr, Ḥāṭib had family and property in Makkah but no tribal protection there. When the Prophet (PBUH) secretly prepared to march on Makkah after the Quraysh violated the Treaty of Ḥudaybiyyah, Ḥāṭib sent a letter through a Quraysh woman informing the Makkans of the Prophet (PBUH)’s plan, hoping this favor would make them protect his relatives.

Allah SWT immediately revealed this betrayal to the Prophet (PBUH) who dispatched companions to intercept the messenger at Rawdat Khākh. They found her, forced her to surrender the hidden letter from her hair braid, and brought it back. When the Prophet confronted Ḥāṭib, he explained that his motive was purely familial protection, not disbelief or treachery.
The Prophet (PBUH) accepted his explanation. In response to this incident, Allah SWT revealed:
“O you who believe, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, showing them affection while they have rejected the truth that has come to you …” (60:1).

translation.text: If they gain the upper hand over you, they would be your ˹open˺ enemies, unleashing their hands and tongues to harm you, and wishing that you would abandon faith.

commentary.text: Allah SWT gives us one reason for not befriending those who are opposed to Islam that is, their hope and wish is that you abandon faith!!
If they gain the upper hand over you, they will use every type of harm in their disposal to hurt you in words and action.

translation.text: Neither your relatives nor children will benefit you on Judgment Day—He will decide between you ˹all˺. For Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

sections.title: 4-6 IBRAHIM AND HIS COMPANIONS ARE AND EXCELLENT EXAMPLE FOR THE BELIEVERS AND PRAYER OF IBRAHIM AND HIS COMPANIONS

translation.text: You already have an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, “We totally dissociate ourselves from you and ˹shun˺ whatever ˹idols˺ you worship besides Allah. We reject you. The enmity and hatred that has arisen between us and you will last until you believe in Allah alone.” The only exception is when Abraham said to his father, “I will seek forgiveness for you,˹” adding, “but˺ I cannot protect you from Allah at all.” ˹The believers prayed,˺ “Our Lord! In You we trust. And to You we ˹always˺ turn. And to You is the final return.

commentary.text: Allah SWT presents Prophet Ibrahim (A.S.) and his followers as the finest example of true faith and loyalty to Him. When their people persisted in disbelief, they openly declared that they disowned them and all false gods besides Allah SWT, establishing a permanent divide in belief until their people accepted Allah SWT alone.
This illustrates the firmness and purity of their devotion, showing that love for Allah SWT cannot coexist with allegiance to disbelief.

The only exception in Ibrahim’s case was his temporary promise to seek forgiveness for his father, which he later retracted once he realized his father was an enemy of Allah SWT—teaching that forgiveness for those who die in shirk is not permitted. Finally, Ibrahim and his followers turned humbly to Allah SWT in prayer, affirming their trust, repentance, and certainty of returning to Him, setting a timeless model for believers to uphold unwavering faith while relying solely on Allah.

translation.text: You certainly have an excellent example in them for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day. But whoever turns away, then surely Allah ˹alone˺ is the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

commentary.text: Certainly, there has been in them an excellent example for you to follow -- for those who look forward to the meeting with Allah SWT and the Last Day and hopeful that Allah SWT will treat him benevolently and help him attain to success in the Hereafter.

Allah SWT has no need of such believers, who profess to believe in His religion as well as maintain friendly relations with His enemies. He is Self Sufficient and not dependent on the people's praising and glorifying Him. If they affirm the faith, they do so not for any good or benefit to Allah SWT rather it is for their own good. BUT they cannot gain anything from their affirmation of the faith until they break off all connections of love and friendship with the enemies of Allah SWT as the Prophet Ibraham (PBUH) and his companions did.

translation.text: ˹In time,˺ Allah may bring about goodwill between you and those of them you ˹now˺ hold as enemies. For Allah is Most Capable. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: Allah SWT offers hope and balance to the believers after instructing them to disassociate from the disbelievers. He reminds them that hearts are in His control, and that enmity can turn into friendship and hatred into affection, for Allah SWT is fully capable of transforming hearts and uniting people after conflict.

This Ayat reflects divine wisdom — that even those once opposed to Islam could later embrace faith or live peacefully with believers, as happened when former enemies of the Prophet (PBUH) in Makkah later entered Islam and became his strongest supporters.
THE PROPHET (PBUH) ALSO CAUTIONED MODERATION IN LOVE AND HATE, AS HUMAN RELATIONS CAN SHIFT BY ALLAH SWT’S WILL.

The Ayat closes by affirming that Allah SWT is Forgiving and Merciful, accepting repentance even from those who once opposed the truth — emphasizing that His mercy and forgiveness extend to all who turn sincerely to Him.

sections.title: 7-9 EXCEPTION TO THE PROHIBITION OF FRIENDSHIP WITH UNBELIEVERS WHO HAD NEITHER FOUGHT AGAINST THE BELIEVERS NOR EXPELLED THEM FROM THEIR HOMES

translation.text: ˹In time,˺ Allah may bring about goodwill between you and those of them you ˹now˺ hold as enemies. For Allah is Most Capable. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and fairly with those who have neither fought nor driven you out of your homes. Surely Allah loves those who are fair.

commentary.text: So as to clear up any doubts or misconceptions re: treatment of disbelievers. The answer is that in this context, the word justice, in fact, has-been used in a special sense. It means:

Justice demands that you should not be hostile to those who are not hostile to you, for it is not justice to treat the enemy and the non-enemy alike. You have every right to adopt a stern attitude towards those who persecuted you for embracing Islam and compelled you to leave your homes and pursued you even after your expulsion.
But as for those who were not partners in persecuting you, you should treat them well and should fulfill the right they have on you because of blood and other relationships.

translation.text: Allah only forbids you from befriending those who have fought you for ˹your˺ faith, driven you out of your homes, or supported ˹others˺ in doing so. And whoever takes them as friends, then it is they who are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers.

commentary.text: These Ayats clarify an important distinction in Islamic guidance on relations with non-Muslims.

The command to sever ties mentioned earlier was not due to mere disbelief, but because of active hostility and oppression against Islam and its followers. Islam does not forbid kindness, justice, or compassion toward non-Muslims who are peaceful and do not fight against the faith.

This balance is beautifully illustrated in the incident of Asma bint Abu Bakr (R.A.) and her mother, Qutaylah bint Abdul Uzza, who was still a disbeliever. When Qutaylah visited her daughter in Madinah with gifts after the Treaty of Hudaibiyah, Asma sought guidance from her husband the Prophet (PBUH) on whether she could meet and treat her kindly. The Prophet (PBUH)instructed her to maintain ties of kinship and treat her kindly.
This ruling established that Muslims are permitted—and even encouraged—to maintain family bonds and show goodness to non-Muslim relatives if they are not enemies of Islam.

This also extends to helping non-hostile non-Muslims in need, including giving charity to poor dhimmis (non-Muslim citizens under Muslim rule). Thus, Islam promotes justice, mercy, and humanity, even toward those outside the faith, while reserving caution only for those who show enmity and aggression.

sections.title: 10-11 WOMEN THAT BECOME BELIEVERS, TEST THEIR IMAN, AND IF YOU FIND THEM TRUTHFUL DO NOT RETURN THEM TO THEIR UNBELIEVING HUSBANDS

translation.text: Believers, when believing women come to you as Emigrants (in the cause of faith), examine them. Allah fully knows (the truth) concerning their faith. And when you have ascertained them to be believing women, do not send them back to the unbelievers. Those women are no longer lawful to the unbelievers, nor are those unbelievers lawful to those (believing) women. Give their unbelieving husbands whatever they have spent (as bridal-dues); and there is no offence for you to marry those women if you give them their bridal-dues. Do not hold on to your marriages with unbelieving women: ask for the return of the bridal-due you gave to your unbelieving wives and the unbelievers may ask for the return of the bridal-due they had given to their believing wives. Such is Allah''s command. He judges between you. Allah is All-Knowing, Most Wise.

commentary.text: Another issue arose after the Peace Treaty regarding women. These Ayats were revealed in the context of the Treaty of Al-Hudaybiyyah, clarifying the rules regarding Muslim women who migrated from Makkah to Madinah after embracing Islam. This is Allah SWT’s command.

Under the treaty’s general terms, anyone making hijra from Mecca to Madina was to be returned. However, Allah SWT made an exception for believing women who migrated for faith, commanding the Muslims to test their sincerity and, if confirmed as true believers, not to return them to the disbelievers. (Confirming faith was necessary because many women made hijra and some could have been spies or migrated for some other reason). FYI - Test her means ask her questions because women should have knowledge about faith.
This was because marriage between a Muslim woman and a disbeliever was no longer lawful — their faith had created a spiritual and legal separation.

The Prophet (PBUH) implemented this ruling when Umm Kulthum bint ‘Uqbah fled to Madinah after the treaty; her brothers demanded her return, but Allah SWT’s revelation abrogated that part of the agreement regarding women.

The believers were instructed to ensure fairness by returning the dowry (mahr) paid by the disbelieving husbands, and they were permitted to marry these believing women after their waiting period (‘iddah) and proper dowry had been given. Likewise, Muslim men were ordered to sever marital ties with disbelieving wives, as exemplified by ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (R.A.), who divorced two idolater wives after this revelation.

The Ayats further established mutual justice — if a Muslim woman left for the disbelievers, her dowry was to be repaid to her Muslim husband, just as the Muslims were to repay what the disbelievers had spent on wives who migrated. Allah SWT declared this to be His wise and just command, ensuring that the believers-maintained faith-based integrity while upholding fairness and reciprocity in social and marital dealings.

Thus, these rulings marked a key step in defining the boundaries of the Muslim community, emphasizing that faith takes precedence over tribal or marital ties, while still preserving justice and dignity for all.

translation.text: And if any of your wives desert you to the disbelievers, and later you take spoils from them, then pay those whose wives have gone, the equivalent of whatever ˹dowry˺ they had paid. And be mindful of Allah, in Whom you believe.

commentary.text: This passage explains the practical implementation of how the issue of dowries (mahr) was to be resolved between Muslims and disbelievers after the migration and during treaty relations.

When Muslim women migrated to Madinah after embracing Islam, their non-Muslim husbands in Makkah demanded the return of their dowries under the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, while Muslim men who had unbelieving wives left behind in Makkah also had dowries owed to them.
The Ayat provided two possible mechanisms to ensure fairness:

1. In the case of treaty relations:
Muslims proposed a mutual settlement — that each side should return the dowries of those spouses who had migrated. However, the disbelievers refused to cooperate. Therefore, Allah SWT commanded that the Muslims collect the equivalent dowries of the emigrant women in Madinah and distribute these among the Muslim men whose wives had been left behind with the pagans. In this way, the financial rights were balanced internally without sending anything to the disbelievers.

2. In the case of no treaty relations:
For those converts who emigrated from non-treaty territories, a reciprocal compensation system was established. The dowry of a Muslim woman who migrated to Madinah was given to the Muslim whose wife remained with the disbelievers. If the total compensation did not balance out, the shortfall was paid from war spoils (ghanīmah). The Prophet (PBUH) ensured that any Muslim deprived of his dowry was compensated before the spoils were distributed, so that justice was maintained.

In essence, this Ayat demonstrates Islam’s principle of fairness in international dealings — balancing rights even across enemy lines, ensuring that no one’s rightful due was lost due to war, migration, or political division. It also reflects the organized financial justice practiced in the early Muslim community, where spiritual allegiance to Islam was balanced with material equity among believers.

sections.title: 12 WOMEN'S BAI'AH (OATH OF ALLEGIANCE)

translation.text: O Prophet! When the believing women come to you, pledging to you that they will neither associate anything with Allah ˹in worship˺, nor steal, nor fornicate, nor kill their children, nor falsely attribute ˹illegitimate˺ children to their husbands, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge, and ask Allah to forgive them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: These Ayats describe the pledge or biaya that the Prophet (PBUH) took from believing women who embraced Islam and migrated to Madinah. This pledge outlined the core moral and spiritual commitments that defined their entry into the faith community.
When women came to the Prophet (PBUH) to give their bay‘ah (pledge of allegiance), they vowed to:
Worship none besides Allah — affirming pure monotheism.
Avoid theft — upholding honesty in all dealings.
Abstain from adultery or fornication (zina) — preserving chastity and family honor.
Refrain from killing their children — rejecting pre-Islamic practices of infanticide and abortion due to fear of poverty.
Avoid slander or false claims about lineage — not attributing illegitimate children to their husbands.
Obey the Prophet (PBUH) in what is right (ma‘ruf) — meaning obedience only in goodness and justice, not in sin or oppression.
The Prophet (PBUH) would accept their verbal pledge without physical contact, declaring: “I have accepted your pledge. “He never shook hands with women, emphasizing modesty and propriety.
The women affirmed these conditions sincerely, understanding them as both a spiritual covenant with Allah SWT and a social code of conduct.

Specific incidents show how these principles were practiced: women promised not to engage in wailing over the dead (a pre-Islamic mourning ritual), not to tear clothes or pull hair in grief, and to remain steadfast in moral discipline.

sections.title: 13 DO NOT BEFRIEND WITH WHOM ALLAH IS ANGRY

translation.text: O believers! Do not ally yourselves with a people Allah is displeased with. They already have no hope for the Hereafter, just like the disbelievers lying in ˹their˺ graves.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 1

In the final Ayat Allah SWT once again warns the believers — just as He did at the beginning of the Surah — not to take as allies or close friends those who have incurred His wrath, meaning disbelievers who opposed revelation and persisted in disbelief.
Allah SWT explains that such people:

Deny Resurrection: the disbelievers do not believe they will ever be raised again. They deny the Hereafter and are only living for this world whereas a Muslims aim in the Hereafter. They fear no consequences thus live according to their own man-made desires and rules, i.e., even the most humane but nevertheless man-made.
Certainty of punishment: for those who have died in disbelief and are lying in their graves. After death they have now lost all hope of mercy or goodness.

Thus, the Surah begins and ends with the same moral principle that a believer’s loyalty must be guided by faith, righteousness, and allegiance to Allah SWT, not by worldly ties or sympathy for those who have rejected Him.
It closes with praise to Allah SWT, who provides guidance and wisdom through His revelation.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah As-Saff was revealed shortly after the Battle of Uhud. The tone and themes reflect the social and spiritual conditions of that period — when the Muslim community was being tested by both external enemies and internal weakness of faith. The Surah addresses sincere believers, hypocrites, and those wavering in their commitment, encouraging steadfastness and sacrifice in the path of Allah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The central message of the Surah and the theme of this entire Juz is regarding supporting, working for and prioritizing the deen. This Surah is an appeal for sincere commitment and unity within and from the community to struggle (jihad) in Allah SWT’s cause. Having the same goal (within the Ummah) and sacrifice is necessary to support the Deen.

Surah As-Saff condemns hypocrisy and weak faith while inspiring believers to sincerity, unity, and active struggle for the truth. It assures that Allah SWT’s religion will prevail, and those who help His cause with conviction will gain both divine favor and everlasting success.

items.text: THE SURAH MOVES THROUGH SEVERAL KEY THEMES:

Condemnation of Hypocrisy (Ayat 2–4)
Allah SWT rebukes those who profess faith but fail to act accordingly. Allah SWT despises the contradiction between word and deed. True believers are praised for standing “like a solid wall” in defense of truth — firm, disciplined, and sincere in battle and belief.

Warning through the Example of Bani Israel (Ayat. 5–7):
The Muslim Ummah is cautioned not to imitate the Israelites, who opposed and maligned their Prophets —Musa and Jesus (PBU Them) — despite recognizing them as messengers of God. Their obstinacy led to spiritual degeneration and loss of divine favor.

Assurance of the Triumph of Islam (Ayat. 8–9):
Despite the conspiracies of Jews, Christians, hypocrites, and pagans, Allah SWT’s Light (guidance) will never be extinguished. The truth brought by His Messenger will ultimately prevail over all religions, regardless of opposition.

Call to Strive and Sacrifice (Ayat10–13):
Believers are urged to strive with their wealth and lives in Allah SWT’s cause. This sincere jihad is the only path to forgiveness, divine pleasure, Paradise, and worldly honor. The promise of victory and success is linked to steadfast faith and selfless struggle.

Call to Be “Helpers of Allah” (Ayat 14):
The Surah concludes by urging the believers to follow the example of the disciples of Jesus (PBUH)— who stood firm as the Ansar of Allah SWT. Similarly, the followers of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) (us the Muslim Ummah) are invited to become Allah SWT’s helpers, ensuring His word triumphs and earning His eternal approval.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: It is from Ayat 9. Jumma means Day of gathering or being together.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The first section ( 1–8) was revealed in 7 A.H., around the time of the conquest of Khaybar—the final major stronghold of the Jews in Arabia. Therefore, the first section was revealed when Jewish power had been decisively crushed.

The second section ( 9–11), however, was revealed much earlier, soon after the Prophet’s Hijrah (migration) to Madinah. The Friday congregational prayer (Salat al-Jumu‘ah) had been established within five days of his arrival, and the incident described in Ayat 11—when people left the Prophet (PBUH)’s sermon to attend a trade caravan—occurred in those early days, before the community had received complete instruction in the etiquette and discipline of religious gatherings.

Thus, Surah Al-Jumu‘ah combines a late Madinan revelation (addressing the Jews after their final defeat) with an early Madinan revelation (instituting and regulating the Friday prayer), forming a single chapter linked by their shared moral lesson: ‘Obedience to divine command and steadfastness in faith take precedence over worldly concerns or inherited privilege.’

front_matter.label: Theme and subject matter
front_matter.text:
There are two distinct sections revealed at different times but joined together because of their moral and spiritual harmony. This Surah is a pair with the previous Surah As Saff. Theme of previous Ayat carried over here as well. Theme of unity of Muslim Ummah, being a Helper of Allah SWT and to never placing the world before worship of Allah SWT.

The first section was revealed after the final downfall of Jewish power in Arabia. For six years the Jews had opposed the Prophet (PBUH) through intrigue, alliances, and warfare — first in Madinah, then through the Confederates in the Battle of the Trench, and finally at Khaybar, after which they surrendered and lived as tenants under Muslim authority. At this point, Allah SWT addressed them one last time in the Quran.

items.text: This address reminds them of three things:
Their rejection of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was based on racial arrogance — they could not accept that a Messenger could arise from the so-called “gentiles.”

They had failed their covenant as bearers of the Torah, behaving like a donkey laden with books — carrying knowledge but not understanding or practicing it. Their delusion of being God’s exclusive favorites blinded them to the reality that divine responsibility depends on obedience, not lineage.

Their fear of death and preference for worldly security over truth exposed their inner guilt and awareness of sin; had they truly been righteous, they would have longed for the meeting with Allah SWT rather than dreading it.

The second section, revealed years later, concerns the Friday congregational prayer (Jumu‘ah) and was attached to this Surah because it offers Muslims a corresponding test to the Jewish Sabbath. When a trade caravan once arrived during the Prophet’s sermon, most of the congregation left the mosque to attend it, leaving only twelve men behind. Allah SWT commanded that once the call to prayer is proclaimed, all worldly business must cease until the prayer concludes. THIS TEACHES MUSLIMS THAT SPIRITUAL DEVOTION TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER MATERIAL GAIN.

By pairing this injunction with the earlier warning to the Jews, the Quran subtly cautions Muslims not to fall into the same spiritual negligence that led to the Jews’ downfall — to value faith over commerce, obedience over arrogance, and sincerity over outward form.
Thus, the two sections together form a powerful moral reminder: DIVINE FAVOR IS NOT INHERITED BUT EARNED THROUGH FAITH, DISCIPLINE, AND WHOLEHEARTED COMMITMENT TO ALLAH SWT’S GUIDANCE.

translation.text: O believers! When the call to prayer is made on Friday, then proceed ˹diligently˺ to the remembrance of Allah and leave off ˹your˺ business. That is best for you, if only you knew.

commentary.text: Al-Jumu`ah (Friday), and the Orders and Etiquette for Friday

Friday, called Al-Jumuʿah (from jamʿ, meaning “gathering”), is the day Muslims come together for worship in the main mosques. It was the day when Allah SWT completed creation, created Adam, and will bring about the Final Hour. Khutba is the main reason or issue.
Among its blessings is a special hour in which every sincere supplication is accepted.

Hadith: Hour does not mean 60 minutes rather a moment in time. Some say the last few minutes before Maghrib. First give salawat to Prophet (PBUH) then praise Allah SWT then make dua. But do not make prayers bec it is a time of prohibition for salah till Maghrib.
Earlier nations were told about Friday but went astray—Jews chose Saturday, Christians chose Sunday—so Allah SWT guided the Muslim Ummah to the true day of gathering.

When the call to prayer (adhan) is made, believers are commanded that must leave all trade and work and hasten—calmly—to the remembrance of Allah SWT, which refers to the Friday sermon (khutbah) and prayer. The command to stop business shows that Jumuʿah is obligatory for adult men who are residents and healthy; women, travelers, and the sick are excused.

Islam teaches etiquette for this day: perform ghusl (bath), wear clean and good clothes, use perfume and siwāk (tooth stick), and go early, walking calmly. Sit close to the imam, listen attentively to the sermon, and avoid talking. Great rewards are promised for coming early—each step brings the reward of fasting and night prayer for a year. In short, Jumuʿah is a weekly day of unity, purification, and remembrance, reminding believers to place faith before commerce and obedience before worldly gain. Gain spiritual uplifting/renewal from the khutba.
Hadith: The Prophet (PBUH) said he considered burning the houses of those who skipped Jumu‘ah without excuse — showing its seriousness.
He warned that missing three consecutive Jumu‘ah prayers without a valid reason can cause Allah SWT to seal a person’s heart, turning it like that of a hypocrite.

When the call for Jumu‘ah is made, Muslims are to stop all trade and hasten to remember Allah SWT through the sermon and prayer. It is a weekly symbol of unity, discipline, and devotion — marking Muslims as a community that puts faith before commerce and obedience before profit.

translation.text: Once the prayer is over, disperse throughout the land and seek the bounty of Allah. And remember Allah often so you may be successful.

commentary.text: This Ayat beautifully balances worship and worldly life. After commanding Muslims to stop all trade and gather for the Friday congregational prayer, Allah SWT now grants them permission to disperse through the land once the prayer is completed and to seek His bounty—that is, to resume work, business, or any lawful pursuit of livelihood.

The command is not an obligation to work but a permission and encouragement to return to normal life while keeping Allah SWT in remembrance. The Ayat also reminds believers to “remember Allah SWT often so you may prosper”, meaning that even while engaging in worldly affairs—buying, selling, or traveling—one should keep Allah SWT in their hearts and tongues.

Success (falāḥ) comes not merely from work or wealth but from maintaining constant awareness of Allah SWT in all circumstances. True remembrance (dhikr) is to remember Him while standing, sitting, and lying down. True prosperity lies in balancing faith, action, and remembrance.

Unlike the Jewish Sabbath or Christian Sunday, Islam does not prescribe Friday as a day of complete rest, but rather as a day of gathering and remembrance—a symbol of the Muslim Ummah’s unity. Once prayer concludes, believers are encouraged to engage productively with the world while retaining a spiritual focus.

commentary.text: The Prohibition of leaving the Masjid while the Imam is delivering the Friday Sermon

This Ayat was revealed after an incident in Madinah that became a key moment in shaping the etiquette of Friday (Jumuʿah) prayer. While the Prophet (PBUH) was delivering the Friday sermon, a trade caravan led by Dihyah bin Khalifah arrived from Syria, accompanied by drums and music to announce its arrival. At that time, the Muslims were still new to Madinah and suffering from economic hardship and scarcity due to the Quraysh blockade. Hearing the drums, many people in the congregation hurried out to the marketplace, leaving the Prophet (PBUH) standing on the pulpit with only twelve companions remaining.

In response, Allah SWT revealed this Ayat to serve as a gentle reprimand and a moral lesson, not a condemnation. It reminded believers that faith and worship must take priority over worldly pursuits—that the reward with Allah SWT is far superior to any material profit or entertainment. The event reflected a momentary weakness caused by difficult circumstances and insufficient training, not hypocrisy or love of the world. Later, the same companions demonstrated extraordinary faith, sacrifice, and dedication to Islam.
The Ayat also established the prohibition of leaving the masjid while the Imam is delivering the khutbah (sermon).

Finally, Allah SWT concludes by reminding believers that true provision and success come only from Him — “Allah is the best of providers.” Worldly sustenance may come through trade, but it is Allah SWT who blesses it and determines its outcome. Thus, this Ayat completes the guidance on Friday worship: when the call to prayer is made, all worldly activity should stop; believers should attend the sermon and prayer with full attention; and after it concludes, they may return to their work — always remembering that spiritual devotion (communal) precedes (personal) material gain, and that what is with Allah SWT lasts far longer than what is in this world.
