front_matter.text: This Surah was sent down either during the Holy Prophet's return journey from his campaign against Bani al- Mustaliq, or immediately after his arrival back at Madinah, in Sha'ban A. H. 6.

items.text: 1. The Rise of Abdullah bin Ubayy

Before the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrated to Madinah, two major tribes — the Aus and the Khazraj — were tired of years of fighting. They had almost agreed to make one man their leader and king: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the chief of Khazraj.
But when Islam spread in Madinah, and many from both tribes accepted the Prophet’s message, the plan to crown Ibn Ubayy ended. His dream of kingship was over. Outwardly he accepted Islam, but deep inside he was full of jealousy and anger toward the Prophet (PBUH).
2. The Beginning of Hypocrisy in Madinah

After the Prophet’s migration (Hijrah), Ibn Ubayy and his followers pretended to be Muslims to protect their status and influence. They prayed, gave zakat, and joined public gatherings, but in their hearts, they disliked Islam and secretly worked against it.
The Quran later described them as munāfiqūn — hypocrites who said they believed but did not truly have faith.
3. Early Acts of Hypocrisy
After the Battle of Badr, when the Prophet (PBUH) punished the Jewish tribe Banu Qaynuqa for breaking their peace agreement, Ibn Ubayy defended them and tried to protect them from justice.

During the Battle of Uhud, when 1,000 Muslims were preparing to fight against 3,000 Quraysh, Ibn Ubayy withdrew with 300 of his men, leaving the Prophet with only 700 fighters. This open betrayal showed his true nature.
After this, many Muslims in Madinah began to recognize that he was not sincere.
4. Continued Plots and Deception
Even after being exposed, Ibn Ubayy continued to make trouble:
He secretly promised support to the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir against the Prophet (PBUH), although Allah SWT revealed his plot in Surah Al-Hashr.
Because he still had many followers among the Aus and Khazraj, the Prophet (PBUH) dealt with him gently and avoided internal conflict for the unity of Madinah.
5. The Incident During the Campaign of Banu al-Mustaliq
The event that led directly to the revelation of Surah Al-Munāfiqūn happened during the Prophet’s campaign against Banu al-Mustaliq (in 5 A.H.).

After victory, while the Muslim army was resting at a well called Al-Muraisi‘, a dispute broke out between a man from the Muhājirīn (Emigrants) and a man from the Ansār (Helpers). Harsh words were exchanged, and both groups called for their supporters.
When the Prophet (PBUH) heard this, he immediately said: “What is this call of ignorance? Leave it, for it is an evil thing.” He stopped the quarrel before it turned into tribal fighting.
6. Ibn Ubayy’s Dangerous Words
Taking advantage of the tension, Ibn Ubayy became angry and said to his people:
“These Emigrants have taken over our city and wealth. When we return to Madinah, the honorable ones will drive out the lowly ones!”

He meant that he and the people of Madinah (the “honorable”) would drive out the Prophet (PBUH) and the Emigrants (the “lowly”).
A young companion, Zayd bin Arqam, heard these words and told the Prophet (PBUH) what Ibn Ubayy had said.
When the Prophet questioned Ibn Ubayy, he denied it and took an oath to try and prove himself as truthful.

Many of the older Ansār supported him, saying Zayd was just a boy. Zayd felt hurt, but Allah SWT soon revealed Ayats confirming the truth of what Zayd had heard — these became part of Surah Al-Munāfiqūn.
7. The Prophet’s Wisdom
When Umar (RA) heard of Ibn Ubayy’s words, he asked permission to kill him, but the Prophet (PBUH) refused, saying: “People will say that Muhammad kills his own companions.”

Instead, he ordered the army to march immediately — an unusual move — so that people would be too busy and tried to spread gossip. Later, when they returned to Madinah, Ibn Ubayy’s own son stood at the gate with his sword and said to his father: “You will not enter Madinah until the Prophet (PBUH) allows it.”
The Prophet permitted him to enter, showing patience and forgiveness.
8. Revelation of Surah Al-Munāfiqūn

At this time, Surah Al-Munāfiqūn was revealed. It exposed the lies of the hypocrites, warned the believers not to be deceived by their wealth and words, and reminded Muslims to remain loyal and sincere to Allah SWT and His Messenger.
Leadership in Islam is not about status or tribe but about sincerity and service.
Hypocrisy can harm a community more than open enemies because it is subtle and secretive.
The Prophet’s patience and wisdom preserved Muslim unity at a critical time.
Allah SWT protects His Messenger by exposing the truth and strengthening the believers.
Faith and obedience must come from the heart, not just from words or actions.

As described in Surah Al Imaran. A person who brings faith in the AM and then denies in the PM. Very few people like that with no faith in their heart at all but they use religion when it suits them and discard when it does not.
Hypocrisy kinds:
Those weak in faith after accepting Iman: Not willing to give their time, energy, wealth and even life.
The hypocrites make excuses and even take false oaths to prove they are believers.
Last stage is when hypocrites target the leader of faith with hatred and resentment.
Most people are just weak in faith as they don’t know any better but once you have joined a movement then you don’t have an option not strive hard.

sections.title: 1-8 HYPOCRITES ARE SUCH ENEMIES OF ISLAM AND MUSLIMS THAT EVEN RASOOL'S PRAYER CANNOT OBTAIN FORGIVENESS FOR THEM FROM ALLAH

arabic_lines: اِذَا جَآءَكَ الۡمُنٰفِقُوۡنَ قَالُوۡا نَشۡهَدُ اِنَّكَ لَرَسُوۡلُ اللّٰهِ ۘ وَاللّٰهُ يَعۡلَمُ اِنَّكَ لَرَسُوۡلُهٗ ؕ وَاللّٰهُ يَشۡهَدُ اِنَّ الۡمُنٰفِقِيۡنَ لَـكٰذِبُوۡنَ

translation.text: (O Prophet), when the hypocrites come to you, they say: “We bear witness that you are certainly Allah's Messenger.” Allah certainly knows that you are His Messenger. But Allah also bears witness that the hypocrites are utter liars!

commentary.text: When the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was in Madinah, the hypocrites used to greet him respectfully and declare, “You are surely the Messenger of Allah.” Their words were true, but their hearts did not believe it. They only said this to appear loyal and to keep their position among the Muslims. Allah SWT affirmed that the Prophet (PBUH) is truly His Messenger, yet He also revealed that these people were liars because their faith was fake.
FYI – There was no hypocrisy in Mecca because to believe meant one had to endure so much opposition and resistance.
THIS AYAT TEACHES THAT ISLAM IS NOT ABOUT OUTWARD STATEMENTS—IT IS ABOUT SINCERITY, HONESTY, AND A HEART THAT TRULY BELIEVES IN WHAT THE TONGUE SAYS.

Refers to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his followers in Madinah, who pretended to be Muslims after the Prophet (PBUH) arrived. They attended prayers and used Islamic language but secretly opposed him to protect their lost power.
Lesson: Hypocrisy creeps in like a black ant on a black cloth in a black night. Slowly and with us even knowing.

translation.text: They have made their ˹false˺ oaths as a shield, hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah. Evil indeed is what they do!

commentary.text: The hypocrites in Madinah used to take oaths — swearing by Allah SWT — to make people believe they were sincere Muslims. These oaths were only shields to protect themselves from being exposed or punished. They are turning away from Allah SWT’s path and stopping others from following it for example, by telling people not to go to war, or give in charity etc.
Ibn Ubayy took a false oath against Zaid when he was exposed. But then Allah SWT revealed the truth

This Ayat especially refers to Abdullah bin Ubayy, who swore falsely to deny his wrongdoing. Such hypocrisy and false oaths, ALLAH SWT SAYS, THESE ARE TRULY EVIL ACTS BECAUSE THEY SPREAD DOUBT, WEAKEN UNITY, AND BLOCK FAITH FROM GROWING.

translation.text: This is because they believed and then abandoned faith. Therefore, their hearts have been sealed, so they do not comprehend.

commentary.text: This Ayat explains that the hypocrites first claimed to believe but then turned back to disbelief in their hearts. They used Islam as a cover instead of accepting it sincerely. Because they chose this path of hypocrisy, Allah SWT sealed their hearts — not as punishment without reason, but because of their own choice. Once their hearts were sealed, they lost the ability to truly understand or feel remorse.
Their lies, deceit, and contradictions between words and actions became normal to them – they became desensitized to their actions.
The Ayat reminds us that when people knowingly reject truth, Allah SWT removes from them the light of guidance and the ability to see right from wrong.

translation.text: When you see them, their appearance impresses you. And when they speak, you listen to their ˹impressive˺ speech. But they are ˹just˺ like ˹worthless˺ planks of wood leaned ˹against a wall˺. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah condemn them! How can they be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

commentary.text: The hypocrites in Madinah looked impressive — strong, handsome, and well-spoken — but their hearts were empty of faith. Allah SWT likened them to useless pieces of wood propped against a wall: they appear solid yet serve no purpose. Their outer charm and polite words hid their inner deceit.
Deep inside, they were full of fear, thinking every sound or event might expose their lies.
Allah SWT warned the Prophet (PBUH) to beware of such people, for they were the most dangerous enemies — those who harm Islam from within.
Lesson: These are the real enemies because they first believed and then are sowing seeds of doubt. Very bad example for others.

translation.text: When it is said to them, “Come! The Messenger of Allah will pray for you to be forgiven,” they turn their heads ˹in disgust˺, and you see them ˹O Prophet˺ turn away in arrogance.

commentary.text: When the Ayats were revealed and Ibn Ubayy’s crimes exposed some companions suggested he go to the Prophet (PBUH) and ask for forgiveness’s, but he refused in pride.

They not only refuse to come to the Messenger (PBUH) to seek forgiveness, but also on hearing the invitation they shake their heads with arrogance and pride, and remain adamant, thinking that it would be disgraceful for them to approach the Messenger (PBUH) to seek forgiveness. This is a clear sign that they are not believers.
Lesson: Arrogance and pride don’t allow people to bow.

translation.text: It is the same whether you pray for their forgiveness or not, Allah will not forgive them. Surely Allah does not guide the rebellious people.

commentary.text: This Ayat tells us that for the hypocrites, it made no difference whether the Prophet (PBUH) prayed for them or not — Allah SWT will not forgive them because they knowingly chose hypocrisy and disbelief. They were not ignorant; they understood the truth but still opposed it out of pride and self-interest. Allah SWT only guides those who want guidance. Those who reject His message and persist in wrongdoing lose the right to be guided. When one crosses limits then Allah SWT leaves them.
Even the Prophet’s compassion and prayers could not benefit such people, if they continued to turn away from Allah’ SWTs mercy.

After Abdullah bin Ubayy and his group repeatedly lied and denied wrongdoing, some Muslims still hoped the Prophet (PBUH) might pray for their forgiveness. Allah SWT made it clear that such prayers would not help — their hearts were sealed and their hypocrisy fixed. A similar message was later repeated more strongly in Surah At-Tawbah (80, 84).

translation.text: They are the ones who say ˹to one another˺, “Do not spend ˹anything˺ on those ˹emigrants˺ with the Messenger of Allah so that they will break away ˹from him˺.” But to Allah ˹alone˺ belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, yet the hypocrites do not comprehend.

commentary.text: Reason: Hypocrites are criticized who advised people not to support “those who are with the Messenger” so that the Emigrants would be forced to disperse. Historically this refers to an episode at the well of al-Muraisīʿ during a military expedition: a water quarrel escalated and ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy — angry at the Muhājirīn — told his followers to stop spending on the Prophet’s companions and boasted that the “mighty” would drive out the “weak” when they returned to Madinah.

Zayd ibn Arqam overheard and reported it; Ibn Ubayy denied it and the community initially sided with him. When Surah al-Munāfiqūn was later revealed, Zayd was vindicated, and the hypocrite’s plot was exposed. The episode teaches that hypocrisy can be subtle and destructive — using economic/social pressure to break solidarity — and that prophetic patience plus divine truth ultimately protects the Ummah.

During the campaign (al-Muraisīʿ) a fight over water led to tension between Emigrants and Helpers. A Helper complained to ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, who angrily told his followers: “Do not spend on those with the Messenger… when we return the mighty will drive out the weak.” How dare they disrespect us the people who gave them shelter. Zayd ibn Arqam heard this, reported it to the Prophet (PBUH), but Ibn Ubayy denied it and many sided with him. Later, when Surah al-Munāfiqūn was revealed, Zayd was publicly vindicated

The hypocrites urged the Ansār not to support the Muhājirīn (those with the Prophet) — hoping that lack of support would force the Emigrants to leave Madinah. Their words reveal the tactic: Use economic pressure and social influence to break the Muslim bond.
Important to note an Islamic State was not formed so no actual step could be taken against ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy.

Lesson: When we spend on others it is an opportunity for us through Allah SWT because the needy will get money from us or someone else. We are just the vessel Allah SWT choose. Our wealth is a loan from Allah SWT to see what we do. If we hoard things we don’t enjoy them.

translation.text: They say, “If we return to Medina, the honourable will definitely expel the inferior.” But all honour and power belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, yet the hypocrites do not know.

commentary.text: After the conflict at the well of al-Muraysīʿ, the leader of the hypocrites, ibn Ubayy boasted that when they returned to Madinah, “the honourable will drive out the lowly,” referring to himself and his group as the honourable and to the Prophet (PBUH) and the believers as the lowly.
Allah SWT immediately corrected this false claim, declaring that all honour belongs only to Allah SWT, His Messenger, and those who believe sincerely.
When This Ayat Was Revealed, Young Zayd Ibn Arqam Was Vindicated For Reporting The Truth And The Hypocrite’s Lies Were Exposed.
The lesson is clear: status and power do not give real honour—only faith, truthfulness, and obedience to Allah SWT do. Allah SWT gives man Honor and Respect and can easily take it away.
FYI - Ibn Ubayy’s son blocked his entry to Madinah until the Prophet permitted him in — showing the social fallout.
Theses 8 Ayats reveal the stages of hypocrisy and to what stage they can reach. Prognosis. A point where there is enmity towards the leaders.
NOW BELOW IS THE PREVENTATIVE OR CURATIVE TREATMENT FOR HYPOCRISY -- PREVENTATIVE (9) and CURATIVE (10)

sections.title: 9-11 LET NOT YOUR RICHES OR CHILDREN DIVERT YOU FROM THE REMEMBRANCE OF ALLAH, LEST YOU BECOME A REAL LOSER

arabic_lines: يٰۤاَيُّهَا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا لَا تُلۡهِكُمۡ اَمۡوَالُكُمۡ وَلَاۤ اَوۡلَادُكُمۡ عَنۡ ذِكۡرِ اللّٰهِۚ وَمَنۡ يَّفۡعَلۡ ذٰلِكَ فَاُولٰٓـئِكَ هُمُ الۡخٰسِرُوۡنَ

translation.text: O believers! Do not let your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. For whoever does so, it is they who are the ˹true˺ losers.

commentary.text: Allah SWT warns believers not to let wealth or children make them forget His remembrance (this is an all-encompassing zikr). Many people become so absorbed in earning, protecting, or enjoying their worldly blessings that they neglect prayer, honesty, and moral responsibility.

This Ayat comes after the story of the hypocrites, showing that love of worldly gain was at the heart of their downfall. Allah SWT reminds us that everything we own and everyone we love are tests, not distractions — and that those who allow worldly ties to replace faith will ultimately be the real losers.
Lesson: PREVENTATIVE FROM INDULGING IN HYPOCRISY IS BUSY YOURSELF IN WORSHIP. Do not let life distract you from your main goal/purpose.

Farhat H recounts the disciplined daily routine of her mother, who raised twelve children. Regardless of how many family members returned home, her mother consistently observed Tahajud prayer each morning, followed by an extended Fajr prayer, Quran recitation, and zikr (including readings from Surah Baqarah and Imran). She then performed the Ishraq prayer, prepared breakfast for the entire household, studied the Quran with her husband, and continued with preparing lunch and dinner.

Learn from this example that life continues but our connection with our Raab cannot take a backseat. Our purpose and goal in life is to worship our Raab. That should keep us busy. Nani was so busy that she never had time for family politics, gossip, idle talk etc.

translation.text: And donate from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you, and you cry, “My Lord! If only You delayed me for a short while, I would give in charity and be one of the righteous.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT urges believers to spend from what He has given them and not delay acts of goodness.

When death approaches, every person who neglected faith or generosity will plead for just a little more time—to give charity, to repent, to live righteously—but it will be too late. The Quran elsewhere repeats this same warning: at death, the wrongdoer cries, “My Lord, send me back so I may do good,” but is told, “No, it is only a word he speaks.” (23 : 99-100)
THIS TEACHES THAT REPENTANCE AND CHARITY MUST BE DONE NOW, WHILE LIFE AND CHOICE REMAIN.
ONCE THE APPOINTED TIME ARRIVES, THERE IS NO DELAY, AND EVERY SOUL WILL FACE THE RESULTS OF ITS ACTIONS.
Lesson: THE CURE FOR INDULGING IN HYPOCRISY IS SPENDING/CHARITY. Take out what you love the most.
Nifaq – Hypocrisy CURE Infaq – Spending

translation.text: But Allah never delays a soul when its appointed time comes. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: When the time of death comes, no one will be granted respite.

items.text: ATTRIBUTES OF A HYPOCRITE

(63:1) (O Prophet), when the hypocrites come to you, they say: “We bear witness that you are certainly Allah's Messenger.” Allah certainly knows that you are His Messenger. But Allah also bears witness that the hypocrites are utter liars!
(63:2) They have made their ˹false˺ oaths as a shield, hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah. Evil indeed is what they do!

Ayat 1 and 2: LIARS who TAKE FALSE OATHS to make others think they believe. Thus, Hypocrites sow disunity and division because they say one thing and then do the other/opposite, spreading doubt/confusion/division/disunity.
They set a bad example and hinder others from following the truth by telling them not to go to war or give in charity.
(63:3) This is because they believed and then abandoned faith. Therefore, their hearts have been sealed, so they do not comprehend.

Ayat 3: BELIEVED THEN REVERTED TO DISBELIEF: Their lies, deceit, and contradictions between words and actions became normal to them – they became desensitized to their actions. Cannot tell truth from falsehood.
They often twist and distort what the Quran says to suit their own needs and requirements so beware.

(63:4) When you see them, their appearance impresses you. And when they speak, you listen to their ˹impressive˺ speech. But they are ˹just˺ like ˹worthless˺ planks of wood leaned ˹against a wall˺. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah condemn them! How can they be deluded ˹from the truth˺?

Ayat 4: THEY LOOK GOOD AND SPEAK WELL but don’t get deceived by their impressive external!  Their entire focus is on themselves. They follow their whims and desires, that is, they sleep, eat, drink, play when and how much they want. Their words are eloquent therefore they lie convincingly. But like dry hollow wood, they are useless, empty, and faithless. Fixed/adamant in their views or attitudes, unbending like dry wood.
THEY ARE AFRAID, DEFENSIVE and constantly on edge in the fear that they may be exposed.
MOST DANGEROUS ENEMY FOR MUSLIMS because they sow divisions and disunity from inside. Do not be their friends or confidant as they will weaken or even destroy your faith.
(63:5) When it is said to them, “Come! The Messenger of Allah will pray for you to be forgiven,” they turn their heads ˹in disgust˺, and you see them ˹O Prophet˺ turn away in arrogance.

(63:8) They say, “If we return to Medina, the honourable will definitely expel the inferior.” But all honour and power belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, yet the hypocrites do not know.
Ayat 5 and 8: PROUD/ARROGANT and never want to accept their faults and DO NOT ASK FOR FORGIVENESS.

They feel they should lead and not follow as was the case with Ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, whose lying and taking a false oath when exposed by Allah SWT Himself, refused to ask for forgiveness.

(63:7) They are the ones who say ˹to one another˺, “Do not spend ˹anything˺ on those ˹emigrants˺ with the Messenger of Allah so that they will break away ˹from him˺.” But to Allah ˹alone˺ belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, yet the hypocrites do not comprehend.

Ayat 7: SELFISH, STINGY, INHOSPITABLE. GOOD MANNERS AND UNDERSTANDING OF DEEN ARE NOT FOUND IN A HYPOCRITE. Not spending and encouraging others not to spend or host.  Hypocrisy can be subtle and destructive by using economic/social pressure to break solidarity. Therefore, the Muslim community and Ummah must beware.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from Ayat 9.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Madani Surah revealed in the early period after the Prophet’s migration. Its themes of faith in creation, accountability, family life, and moral conduct show a blend of Makkan spirituality and Madinan community guidance, reflecting Islam’s transition from belief to practical living.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah At-Taghabun teaches that real profit and real loss are not what people perceive in this world, but what will be revealed in the Hereafter. It contrasts faith and disbelief, showing that true success lies in believing in Allah SWT and obeying His Messenger (PBUH) while true loss belongs to those who deny and disobey. 

The Surah emphasizes personal accountability and warns that wealth and family can distract from obedience, turning apparent worldly gain into spiritual loss. It also calls believers to patience in hardship, trust in Allah SWT, and spending in His cause, explaining that trials are part of a divine test. 

In essence, At-Taghābun redefines gain and loss by shifting focus from temporary worldly outcomes to eternal consequences.

translation.text: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Allah. The kingdom is His, and all praise is for Him. For He is Most Capable of everything.
He is the One Who created you, yet some of you are disbelievers while some are believers. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.

commentary.text: Allah SWT reminds mankind that He alone is their Creator, yet people are divided — some choose to believe, while others deny the truth. He has given everyone the ability to choose freely, and each person is responsible for that choice.

Human nature itself was created pure and inclined toward belief (fitra), but arrogance, ignorance, or external influences can corrupt it. Allah SWT sees all that people do, meaning that He observes their actions, intentions, and choices — and will reward or punish accordingly. This Ayat teaches that faith is not forced but chosen, and that the gift of life itself is proof enough to recognize and obey the Creator.

translation.text: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. He shaped you ˹in the womb˺, perfecting your form. And to Him is the final return.

commentary.text: Allah SWT has created the heavens and the earth with truth, meaning everything was made with purpose, justice, and wisdom. Nothing in creation is meaningless or accidental.  Creation with wisdom implies a Day of Judgment where humans—given freedom and responsibility—will answer for how they used their gifts. Accountability must come after life’s full effects are complete, which is why it will occur in the next world when all generations are gathered.
He also shaped human beings in the best form—giving them upright bodies, intellect, conscience, and free will to choose between right and wrong.
Allah SWT mentions His favours upon us so we may be grateful.

translation.text: He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal. For Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.

commentary.text: Allah SWT knows not only what people do outwardly but also their hidden motives and intentions. He alone can see the difference between an action done in sincerity and one done with deceit. This awareness makes Allah SWT the only Being capable of absolute justice. Human courts, no matter how advanced, can judge only what is seen or proven; they cannot know the secrets of the heart.

Many crimes remain hidden, and many guilty people escape punishment. Therefore, true justice requires an all-knowing Judge and a Day when every deed and motive will be revealed — the Hereafter. The Quran explains that since Allah SWT created the heavens and the earth “with truth,” justice must prevail, and that is only possible in His court. To deny Allah SWT or the Hereafter is to assume that our universe is unjust and meaningless — a conclusion both irrational and morally empty.

translation.text: Have the stories of those who disbelieved before not reached you ˹pagans˺? They tasted the evil consequences of their doings, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is informing us about the past nations and the torment and disciplinary lessons that they suffered because of opposing the Messengers and denying the truth.
Here again we are being reminded that Allah SWT has favoured us so much with Islam so if we deny then we must be prepared to suffer the consequences.

translation.text: That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said ˹mockingly˺, “How can humans be our guides?” So they persisted in disbelief and turned away. And Allah was not in need ˹of their faith˺. For Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

commentary.text: This Ayat explains why past nations were destroyed: when messengers came with clear and logical proofs from Allah SWT, the people arrogantly said, “Can mere humans guide us?” They forgot that Allah SWT sends guidance through His chosen human messengers, not angels or idols.

Their pride led them to reject the truth, and so Allah SWT left them to their misguidance. He is Self-Sufficient and does not need anyone’s faith or praise; His guidance is for people’s own good. When they turn away from it, they only harm themselves.
Lesson: Mocking, Pride, and Persistent disbelief lead to Ruin.

translation.text: The disbelievers claim they will not be resurrected. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will certainly be informed of what you have done. And that is easy for Allah.”

commentary.text: This Ayat answers those who deny life after death. They stubbornly claim there will be no resurrection, though they have no evidence for it. The Prophet (PBUH) is told to reply with conviction: “Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be raised.”

The Ayat explains that resurrection is both necessary and easy for Allah SWT. It is necessary because justice demands that every human be held accountable for their deeds; and it is easy because the same God who created the universe and gave life in the first place can surely bring it back again. Denying the Hereafter means believing that this purposeful world ends without justice—a belief both irrational and self-defeating.

translation.text: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and in the Light We have revealed. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: Therefore, believe in Allah and in His Messenger and in the Light which We have sent down. that is, the Quran.  Again we are remined that Allah is All-Aware of what you do. none of your deeds ever escapes His knowledge.

translation.text: ˹Consider˺ the Day He will gather you ˹all˺ for the Day of Gathering—that will be the Day of mutual loss and gain. So whoever believes in Allah and does good, He will absolve them of their sins and admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. That is the ultimate triumph.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = ETERNAL SUCCESS

This Ayat describes the Day of Resurrection, called Yawm at-Taghābun (ghabaan)—the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain—when all humanity will be gathered before Allah SWT. On that day, the reality of every person’s action will be laid bare: those who followed truth will see their eternal reward, and those who rejected faith will realize their great loss.

It will also be a day of perfect justice, when every wrong will be repaid; good deeds will be taken from oppressors and given to the wronged, and false friendships based on sin will turn into blame and enmity. The Ayat teaches that true faith means believing in Allah SWT as He revealed through His Messenger and living by His guidance. Those who do so will have their sins forgiven and will dwell forever in gardens beneath which rivers flow—this is the real and lasting victory, far beyond any success of this world.
Everyone is allotted a place in Hell or Heaven.

‘The Day of Mutual loss’, does not mean both end up in Hell. It means both sides discover a loss happened in the exchange, even though one side ultimately gains. “mutual” here is in exposure, not in outcome.
Human thinking: winner vs loser. Quran thinking who wasted what they were given.

translation.text: As for those who disbelieve and reject Our revelations, they will be the residents of the Fire, staying there forever. What an evil destination!

translation.text: No calamity befalls ˹anyone˺ except by Allah’s Will. And whoever has faith in Allah, He will ˹rightly˺ guide their hearts ˹through adversity˺. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed when the early Muslims faced intense hardship — persecution, exile, poverty, and constant danger. Allah SWT reminds them that every trial happens only with His permission and for a wise purpose. True faith helps a believer stay steady and hopeful through adversity.
Nothing happens by chance or by the power of people; every event follows a divine plan meant for the believer’s ultimate good.

Allah SWT knows exactly what each believer endures and never leaves them unsupported. Every hardship is either a means of purification, reward, or hidden mercy — and for the believer, every outcome becomes good.

① Afflictions by Allah SWT’s leave: Hardships are never random; no person or power can harm without Allah’s will. Each difficulty serves a divine purpose that human minds may not immediately grasp.
② Faith and guidance: When a believer trusts Allah SWT, his heart remains firm, patient, and content; instead of despair and pain, he finds inner peace and purpose. Always so good words even in times of severe tests. 
③ Allah SWT’s knowledge: Allah SWT knows the state and sincerity of every believer and tailors each test to his strength and growth.
Very Important Ayat!

translation.text: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger! But if you turn away, then Our Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.

commentary.text: Whatever the circumstances, good or bad, you should remain steadfast to obedience to Allah SWT and His Messenger. But if under the pressure of hardships you turned away from obedience, you would only harm your own selves. The only responsibility of Our Messenger was to guide you to the right path, which the Messenger has fulfilled in the best way possible.

Therefore, whoever believes sincerely that Allah SWT is One, has no other choice than to place his full trust in Him and to continue doing his duty as a believer with the conviction that goodness and well-being only lie in the way that Allah SWT has shown him.

translation.text: O believers! Indeed, some of your spouses and children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive ˹their faults˺, then Allah is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: The Ayat teaches balance: believers must beware of letting family ties weaken their faith, yet they must not become harsh or cruel. Instead, they should forgive, overlook mistakes, and act kindly, for Allah is Merciful.

Allah SWT cautions believers that sometimes even those dearests to them — their spouses or children — can unknowingly become their enemies by distracting them from the path of obedience. This happened to some early Muslims who delayed migration to Madinah because their families held them back, and they later regretted it. So Allah SWT sent this Ayat to forgive them, and Allah SWT will forgive you. (BEAUTIFUL)

True success is built on four connected principles: (i) striving for taqwa within one’s ability, (ii) obeying divine guidance (action), (iii) giving in charity, and (iv) overcoming inner greed.

Allah SWT does not demand perfection but sincere effort, linking ideal God-consciousness with human capacity. Obedience ensures faith turns into action, while charity purifies both the heart and society and benefits the giver in the Hereafter. The Ayat defines real prosperity not by what a person possesses, but by being saved from selfish attachment and learning to give for Allah SWT’s sake.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The Surah takes its name from the very first word “At-Talaq” (الطلاق), meaning divorce.
It is also known as “Surah an-Nisā’ al-Qusra” — “The Shorter Surah of Women”, because it serves as a concise supplement to Surah an-Nisā’ and Surah al-Baqarah both of which also contain rulings on family life, marital relations, and women’s rights.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah At-Talaq was revealed after Surah Al-Baqarah (2:228–234) in which the laws of divorce (ṭalāq) and waiting periods (ʿiddah) were first laid down.

After the initial rulings of Surah Al-Baqarah were revealed, many people misunderstood or misapplied them in practice. Some men would pronounce divorce in a hasty or unjust manner or violate the prescribed waiting periods and rights of women.

Therefore, Allah SWT revealed Surah At-Talaq to clarify, correct, and complete the earlier instructions — providing a more detailed and balanced procedure to regulate the matter of divorce with justice and compassion.

front_matter.label: Overview and Background
front_matter.text: Surah At-Talaq is a Medinan Surah revealed to clarify and regulate the proper procedure and ethics of divorce in Islam. It does not abolish or alter the divorce laws already revealed in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:228–234) and Surah Al-Ahzab (33:49), but rather supplements and refines them — ensuring justice, compassion, and restraint in family matters.

front_matter.label: The Qur’anic Instructions on Divorce and Iddah
front_matter.text: Before this Surah, the Quran had already laid down several key rulings on ṭalāq (divorce) and ʿiddah (waiting period):

items.text: Number of Divorces

“Divorce may be pronounced twice; then the wife may either be kept back in fairness or allowed to separate in fairness.” (2:229)
A man may pronounce at most three divorces. After the first or second, reconciliation is possible within the waiting period. After the third, remarriage is not permissible unless the woman marries another man and is later divorced by him naturally (tahlīl).
Waiting Period for Divorced Women

“Divorced women must wait for three monthly courses…” (2:228)
The waiting period (ʿiddah) of a menstruating, consummated marriage is three menstrual cycles.
No Waiting Period if Marriage Not Consummated
“When you marry believing women and divorce them before touching them, there is no waiting period…” (33:49)
Waiting Period for Widows
“Those of you who die and leave behind wives should instruct them to wait four months and ten days.” (2:234)

Surah At-Talaq is not simply a legal code; it is a moral guide to preserving family harmony and ensuring fairness when separation becomes inevitable.
Its ultimate message is that divine guidance governs even the most private matters — reminding believers that justice, mercy, and God-consciousness are the cornerstones of all human relationships.

front_matter.label: Previous Ayats regarding Divorce
front_matter.text: In order to understand the commandments of this Surah, it would be useful to refresh one's memory about the instructions which have been given in the Quran concerning divorce and the waiting period

items.text: "And the divorced women (after the pronouncement of divorce) must wait for three monthly courses... and their husbands are fully entitled to take them back (as their wives) during this waiting period, if they desire reconciliation." (Al Baqarah 228)

The waiting period of the woman is that she should go through three monthly cycles. The waiting period in case of one or two divorces is that the woman is still the legal wife of the husband and he can take her back as his wife within the waiting period. But if the husband has pronounced three divorces, this waiting period cannot be taken advantage of for the purpose of reconciliation, but it is only meant to bar/ban the woman from re-marrying another person till she finishes her iddah (waiting period).
"Divorce may be pronounced twice; then the wife may either be kept back in fairness or allowed to separate in fairness." (Al Baqarah 229)
A man can pronounce three divorces on his wife. (Maximum limit).

In case the husband has pronounced one or two divorces he is entitled to take back his wife within the waiting period and if after the expiry of the waiting period the two desire to re-marry, they can re- marry. But if the husband has pronounced three divorces, he forfeits his right to keep her as his wife within the waiting. period, and they cannot re-marry unless the woman re-marries another husband who then divorces her of his own free.
"Then, if the husband divorces his wife (for the third time), she shall not remain lawful for him after this divorce, unless she marries another husband..." (Al-Baqarah :230)
"When you marry the believing women, and then divorce them before you have touched them, they do not have to fulfill a waiting period, the completion of which you may demand of them." (Al-Ahzab :49)
There is no waiting period for the woman with whom marriage has not been consummated meaning she is divorced even before she is touched. She can re-marry, if she likes, immediately after the divorce.
"And if those of you who die, leave wives behind, the women should abstain (from marriage) for four months and ten days." (Al-Baqarah: 234)
The waiting period of the woman whose husband dies, is four months and ten days. (widow).

“But if they the married couple separate by way of divorce God will compensate each of them from the need of the other out of His plenty that is out of His bounty by giving her another as husband and giving him another as wife.” (Surah Nisa: 4:130)

Here, one should understand well that Surah At- Talaq was not sent down to annul or amend any of the previous rules rather it was sent to provide answers to questions that had remained after the revelation of the commandments in Surah Al-Baqarah.

So, answers have been supplied to the following questions: (i) What is the waiting period for a woman who has consummated marriage but no longer menstruates, or has not yet menstruated? (ii) What is the waiting period for a woman, who is pregnant, or her husband dies? (iii) And what arrangements would be made for the maintenance and lodging of the different categories of divorced women, and for the raising of the child whose parents are divorced

Talaq literally means untying a knot. Nikkah is the tying of a knot and making each other halal for one another by making Allah SWT a witness. Nikkah is a very unique, intimate, close bond with rights and responsibilities. Like a dress or cloth that covers, protects and comforts. One does not feel exposed or vulnerable with a spouse. But when the trust and intimacy of love is not there and differences become irreconcilable and marriage is a source of constant friction/distress then Allah SWT has legitimized a way out – Talaq. Divorce is not a sin but a part of our deen. Divorce is a very emotional time therefore whoever fears Allah SWT then Allah SWT will bring a way out and provide solutions, bring relief and healing.

The dominant spiritual theme that is emphasized in the Quran when discussing marriage and divorce is taqwa (love and fear of Allah SWT) and tawakkul (hope from Allah SWT). Because often during a divorce when tensions run high due to anxiety and uncertainty taqwa and tawakkul go out the window. There is anger and rage towards the other. People are now thinking about themselves first and all the time.
Thus, the first line of medication is taqwa and tawakkul.
TAQWA: Means "forbearance, fear and abstinence."  Other descriptions include: "God consciousness ... piousness, fear of Allah, love for Allah, and self-restraint".
At its root, the Arabic word “Taqwa” is derived from “وقي” (wa-qa-ya), meaning “to shield” or “to guard”. Linguistically, it suggests the idea of protection or being cautious.

Hadith: It was reported that ‘Umar ibn Khattab (radiyallahu ‘anhu) asked Ubayy ibn Ka’b (radiyallahu ‘anhu) about Taqwa. In reply Ka’b (radiyallahu ‘anhu) asked ‘Umar (radiyallahu ‘anhu), “O Leader of the believers, what do you do when you have to pass through a thorny road?” ‘Umar (radiyallahu ‘anhu) replied, “I lift my cloth up to my calves and watch my footsteps and take each step slowly from the fear of thorns lest they don’t prick me”. Ka’b (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said, “This is Taqwa”.
Thus, navigating this world with caution that is, carefully and consciously taking one step at a time.
TAWAKKUL: Means (Arabic: تَوَكُّل)  "to put trust" or " reliance on God” or "trusting in God's plan".

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “If you all depend on Allah SWT with due reliance, He would certainly give you provision as He gives it to birds who go forth hungry in the morning and return with [a] full belly at dusk.” This hadith teaches us that tawakkul begins with the heart's firm reliance on Allah.

sections.title: 1-7 LAWS OF DIVORCE AND IDDAT (WAITING PERIOD) BEFORE THE DIVORCE TAKE EFFECT AND IDDAT (WAITING PERIOD) IS THREE MENSTRUATION PERIODS OR THREE MONTHS AND DELIVERY IN CASE OF PREGNANCY

translation.text: O Prophet! ˹Instruct the believers:˺ When you ˹intend to˺ divorce women, then divorce them with concern for their waiting period, and count it accurately. And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not force them out of their homes, nor should they leave—unless they commit a blatant misconduct. These are the limits set by Allah. And whoever transgresses Allah’s limits has truly wronged his own soul. You never know, perhaps Allah will bring about a change ˹of heart˺ later.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed about ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar who divorced his wife while she was in her menses. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH), ordered him to take her back and keep her until the period of her menses was over and then wait again until she was in her menses. When she became pure, he was free to divorce her provided that he did not sleep with her before that. And this was the waiting period which Allah SWT has commanded us to observe”.
This commandment lays down two rules simultaneously.

Firstly, men should divorce their wives at a time when their waiting period (iddah) can begin. The waiting period of the married woman who menstruates is three monthly cycles after the pronouncement of divorce.
(Already prescribed in Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 228.)

Therefore, in view of this commandment the only appropriate time of pronouncing divorce -- so that the waiting period may duly begin -- is when a woman is not on her cycle so as not to extend her waiting period to four courses instead of three cycles.
This is to prevent impulsive pronouncements of divorce at the first sign of a fight or issue. A man should be deliberate/mindful of the rules of iddah before declaring divorce.
Additionally, during periods a woman is emotionally unstable and a husband and wife are not allowed to be intimate. So, this is not the time to give divorce.

Furthermore, this commandment also demands that the woman should not be divorced in the period of purity during which the husband may have had sexual intercourse with her. For in this case neither the husband nor the wife can know whether she has conceived or not.
This prescribed waiting period, applies only to those women who have consummated the marriage, who menstruate and thus may possibly conceive.

Do not pronounce three divorces all at once leading to permanent separation, but pronounce one, or at the most two divorces, and wait till the end of the waiting period, so that there remains some chance for reconciliation for you at any time during this period.

Do not treat divorce lightly; it is a grave matter, which gives birth to many legal questions for the man, the woman, their children and the people of their house. Therefore, when divorce is pronounced, its time and date should be remembered and also the state in which divorce was pronounced on the woman; one should keep an accurate account of when the waiting period started and when it would expire.
These are the limits set by Allah. And whoever transgresses Allah’s limits has truly wronged his own soul…

The phrase حُدُودَ اللَّـهِ (the limits set or prescribed by Allah SWT) refers to the sacred laws set down by the Shari’ ah of Islam. The phrase وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ (And whoever exceeds or transgresses the limits prescribed by Allah SWT) implies ‘whoever violates the sacred laws. The phrase فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ (wrongs his own soul) implies that he/she has not damaged Allah’ s sacred laws or the Shari’ ah. In fact, he/she has only caused loss to himself or herself.
A Divorced Woman does not have a Right to Provisions and Accommodations from the Husband

Hadith: When Fatimah bint Qays Fihriyah’s husband Abu Amr bin Hafs divorced her the third and final time.
He was away from her in Yemen at the time, and he sent her his decision to divorce her. He also sent some barley with his messenger, but she did not like the amount or method of compensation. He said, "By Allah I am not obligated to spend upon you." So, she went to Allah's Messenger, who said, there is no obligation on him to spend on you nor housing.

Thus, spending and housing are required from the husband who can return to his wife (after the first and second divorce). So, if he does not have the right to return to her, then she does not have the right to provisions and housing.

This Ayat was revealed to clarify the correct Islamic method of divorce thus sets the rule that divorce should be given at a proper, pure time—allowing the waiting period (ʿiddah) to start correctly and leaving space for fairness and possible reconciliation.
Give divorce at the right time – during a period of purity (not menstruation) and only if no intercourse has occurred, or when pregnancy is known.
Pronounce one divorce – not three at once, so reconciliation remains possible. FYI – Does Talaq bidih (sayig it three times) still count as divorce? As proven by Hadith it is counted as one.
Count the ʿiddah (waiting period) carefully.
Do not expel divorced women from their homes, and they must not leave during ʿiddah—except for open indecency.
Respect Allah’s limits – whoever crosses them harms himself; maybe Allah will bring reconciliation afterward.
Here’s a simple and precise summary of Surah At-Talaq (65:1):
Divorce only when the wife is pure (not menstruating) and no intercourse has occurred in that purity, or when pregnancy is known.
Give one divorce, not three at once — to allow reconciliation.
The wife must stay in her home during the ʿiddah (waiting period); the husband must provide for her if the divorce is revocable. The husband must stay in the house as well.
She may leave only if she commits clear indecency (fāḥishah mubayyinah).
These are Allah’s limits — whoever crosses them harms himself.
Staying together in ʿiddah allows a chance for Allah SWT to bring reconciliation.

translation.text: Then when they have ˹almost˺ reached the end of their waiting period, either retain them honourably or separate from them honourably. And call two of your reliable men to witness ˹either way˺—and ˹let the witnesses˺ bear true testimony for ˹the sake of˺ Allah. This is enjoined on whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them,

commentary.text: Ordaining Kindness towards Divorced Women

When a man has pronounced one or two revocable divorces, then he should make a decision --before the expiry of the waiting-period – that is, whether he would like to keep his wife in wedlock or not. If he decides to keep her, then he should keep her with honor and dignity and not with a view to tormenting and harassing her and getting another opportunity to prolong her waiting-period by divorcing her once again; and if he decides to part with her, then he should part with her gracefully, without indulging in any quarrel or vilification.
If a man still owes her the dowry (mehr), or a part of it, pay it off, and give her something in addition at her departure -- according to your means.
And call to witness two men both at divorce and at reconciliation.

Hadith: Imran bin Husain was asked: A man divorced his wife and then took her back, but he neither called anybody to witness pronouncement of the divorce nor resumption of the relation. He replied: You pronounced the divorce against the sunnah and you took your wife back against the sunnah.
Also see Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 282 where Allah SWT says to have witnesses in case of commercial transactions.

Allah SWT says that whoever acts in fear of Him, He will open for him/her a way out of difficulties. This automatically gives the meaning that whoever does not fear Allah SWT in these matters, will create for himself/herself such complications and difficulties from which he/her will find no way out.

The instructions given above are in the nature of advice and not law. If a man pronounces divorce against the approved method as explained above, or fails to calculate the waiting-period accurately, or expels the wife from the house without a good reason, or returns to her at the end of the waiting period only to harass her, or sends her away after a quarrel, or fails to call men to witness the divorce, reconciliation, or separation, then it will not affect the legal outcomes of divorce or reconciliation or separation. However, his acting against Allah’s advice would be a proof that his heart was devoid of faith in Allah SWT and the Last Day. That is why he adopted a course which a true believer would never adopt.

When the waiting period (ʿiddah) is near its end, the husband must decide clearly to either keep his wife with respect and intention to live well together. Or separate honorably, paying her dues and without quarrel or harm.
Two trustworthy witnesses should be called at the time of divorce, reconciliation, or final separation, to avoid later disputes — this is advised, not a strict condition.
These are moral instructions for those who believe in Allah and the Last Day — disobeying them does not cancel the divorce but shows weak faith.
Fearing Allah SWT in this process — acting fairly, counting the waiting period properly, avoiding harm, and following the Sunnah method — brings ease and a way out of difficulty.
Rushing or violating Allah’s limits (like giving triple divorce at once) leads to confusion and regret, while taqwā (God-consciousness) leads to peace and right outcomes.

translation.text: and provide for them from sources they could never imagine. And whoever puts their trust in Allah, then He ˹alone˺ is sufficient for them. Certainly Allah achieves His Will. Allah has already set a destiny for everything.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed about ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī. His son had been captured by the idolaters, and he came to the Prophet (PBUH) complaining of poverty and distress. The Prophet (PBUH) advised him and his wife to “fear Allah and keep saying ‘Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh’ (There is no power nor might except with Allah)”. They obeyed, and soon Allah caused the enemy to abandon or ignore their son; the young man escaped and returned home driving a flock of about four thousand sheep.

Another narration says the Ayat was revealed about a poor man from the tribe of Ashjaʿ who also sought help from the Prophet (PBUH). The Prophet told him, “Fear Allah and be patient.” Shortly afterward, the man’s captive son returned with a large herd of sheep, and the Prophet (PBUH) told him to keep them.
Meaning: Whoever truly has taqwā (fear of Allah), trusts Him, and obeys His commands, Allah will open unexpected doors of relief and provide from unseen sources.

Whoever has Tawakkul of Allah SWT in what He has commanded and avoids what He has forbidden, then Allah SWT will make a way out for him/her from every difficulty and will provide for him/her from resources he/she never anticipated or thought about.

Lesson: Whoever divorces as Allah commanded him, then Allah will make a way out for him.

Hadith: Ibn Abbas said that he rode the Prophet's camel while sitting behind the Prophet, and the Messenger of Allah said to him, I will teach you words (so learn them).
- Be mindful of Allah SWT and He will protect you.

- If you ask, ask Allah SWT and if you seek help then seek it from Allah SWT.

translation.text: As for your women past the age of menstruation, in case you do not know, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated as well. As for those who are pregnant, their waiting period ends with delivery. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make their matters easy for them.

commentary.text: Reason: This Ayat was revealed in response to a question raised by some Companions after the revelation of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:228). They asked the Prophet (PBUH) about the waiting period for three categories of women not mentioned in that verse—the elderly whose menstruation had ceased, the young who had not yet menstruated, and those who were pregnant. Allah then revealed this verse, addressing all three situations and completing the law.

This Ayat explains the rules of ‘iddah—the waiting period a woman must observe before remarrying after divorce or the death of her husband. Allah SWT clarifies that women who have reached menopause and no longer menstruate must observe a waiting period of three lunar months, instead of the three menstrual cycles prescribed for women who still experience menses (as mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:228).
The same rule applies to young girls who have not yet begun menstruation—their ‘iddah is also three months.

The phrase “if you have doubt” (إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ) has been understood in two ways: some early scholars said it refers to uncertainty about whether bleeding is menstrual or not, while others say that it addresses those unsure about the ruling itself. The second view is more evident, as it concludes the guidance that might have been previously unclear.
Allah SWT further states that pregnant women’s ‘iddah ends when they give birth, regardless of whether their husbands divorced them or passed away.

The Ayat conclude with Allah’s promise: “And whoever fears Allah, He will make his matter easy for him.” This links legal rulings with spiritual benefit, reminding believers that those who observe divine guidance with taqwā (piety) will find ease, relief, and facilitation from Allah in their affairs.

Thus, these Ayat not only outline precise legal rulings for different categories of women but also emphasize that obedience to Allah’s laws brings spiritual and worldly ease, completing both the legal and moral dimensions of family life in Islam.

Women who have not started menses as well as those who no longer menstruate and have reached menopause then their waiting-period will be from the day divorce was pronounced on them and three months imply three lunar months.
As for those who are pregnant, their waiting period ends with delivery.
And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make their matters easy for them.

translation.text: This is the commandment of Allah, which He has revealed to you. And whoever is mindful of Allah, He will absolve them of their sins and reward them immensely.

commentary.text: This is His commandment and legislation that He sent down to you through His Messenger, and whosoever has Taqwa of Allah, , Allah will prevent what he fears and multiply his reward even for the little good he does.

Obviously, the waiting period of the divorced woman whose term has been prescribed as three months will be longer than that of the woman whose term has been appointed as three menstruations, and the term of the pregnant woman may be several months longer.

To shoulder the responsibility of the maintenance and lodging of the woman whom a man may have decided to give up, during this whole period might be an unbearable burden for some, but Allah SWT’s promise is that He will lighten the burden for those who fear Him and follow His commands.  And Allah SWT will reward the person much more generously and richly in comparison to the small burden borne by him/her in this world.

translation.text: Let them live where you live ˹during their waiting period˺, according to your means. And do not harass them to make their stay unbearable. If they are pregnant, then maintain them until they deliver. And if they nurse your child, compensate them, and consult together courteously. But if you fail to reach an agreement, then another woman will nurse ˹the child˺ for the father.

commentary.text: Allah SWT commands that when a man divorces his wife, he must provide her with decent accommodation during her waiting period (ʿiddah) according to his means — even if it is only a small space.
The husband must live in the house as well so that if there is to be a reconciliation then it is possible.
He must not harm, harass, or pressure her to leave or to give up her rights.
If the divorced woman is pregnant, the husband must support her financially until she gives birth.
After the child is born and the ʿiddah ends, if the mother nurses the baby, she has the right to be paid for nursing.
Both parents must deal fairly and kindly with one another for the child’s welfare.
If they disagree about payment, the father may arrange for another woman to nurse the child; but if the mother later accepts the same fair rate, she has priority to nurse her own child.

Although this is a general counsel which applies to all matters and conditions of human life, yet in this particular context the objective is to warn Muslims to follow the commands mentioned above in fear of God, no matter what, for as a reward for this Allah SWT will remove their troubles, forgive their sins and enhance their rewards in the Hereafter – in sha Allah.

A man who has divorced his wife but still is in the probationary period before the divorce becomes absolute then he must provide for her with residence and maintenance on the same scale as himself, meaning according to his status in life. There is still hope of reconciliation and if not, the parting must be honorable.

If there is a pregnancy and therefore added responsibility (perhaps also added hope for reconciliation) for both parents. In this case no separation is possible until after the child is born. Even after birth, if no reconciliation between parents is possible, still the nursing of the child and the welfare of the child and the care of the mother remains the duty of the father via mutual counsel between the parents in all truth and sincerity. The best welfare of the child should be kept the priority.
Also see Surah Baqarah Ayat 233

Divorced˺ mothers will breastfeed their offspring for two whole years, for those who wish to complete the nursing ˹of their child˺. The child’s father will provide reasonable maintenance and clothing for the mother ˹during that period˺. No one will be charged with more than they can bear. commentary.text: Allah SWT commands that the wealthy should spend according to their means, and those with limited resources should spend as much as Allah has provided them.
“Allah SWT does not burden a person beyond what He has given him.” This means everyone is responsible only within their capacity — no one is asked to give more than they can afford.

Allah promises that after hardship comes ease, and His promise is always true. Just as He says elsewhere:
“Indeed, with every hardship there is relief.” (Surah Ash-Sharh 94:5–6)

The wealthy father should spend on the child according to his means and the man whose resources are restricted, should spend him spend according to what Allah SWT has given him. Allah SWT puts no burden on any person beyond what He has given him.
….After hardship, Allah will bring about ease….

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah’s name is from the very first Ayat.  The name At-Tahrim (“The Prohibition) refers to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) making something lawful forbidden for himself.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Historical events almost precisely determine that this Surah was sent down sometime during A.H. 7 or A. H 8. The Surah was revealed during the later Madinan period, when both Safiyyah (r.a.) and Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (r.a.) were part of the Prophet’s household.

items.text: This Surah discusses important moral and spiritual lessons arising from incidents involving the Prophet’s (PBUH) wives. It emphasizes first that only Allah SWT has the power to declare what is lawful or unlawful.
Secondly, it highlights that the life of a Prophet (PBUH) is under divine supervision—even his smallest actions are corrected by Allah SWT so that the religious law remains pure and unaltered.

Thirdly, this correction assures believers that everything in the Prophet’s (PBUH) practice and teachings that remained uncriticized by Allah SWT is perfectly in harmony with divine will, and thus a fully reliable model for guidance.
Fourthly, Allah SWT’s gentle reproach of the Prophet (PBUH) and firm warning to his wives demonstrates that, though deeply revered, they were human and could err.

Other examples from various Surahs show this balance. In Surah Āl-ʿImrān (3:152), Allah reminded the Muslims of their weakness at Uhud; in Surah An-Nūr, He corrected the community’s reaction to the slander against ʿĀ’ishah; in Surah Al-Aḥzāb, He advised the Prophet’s wives about choosing between worldly comfort and devotion; in Surah Al-Jumuʿah, He reproved the Companions for leaving the Friday sermon for trade; and in Surah Al-Mumtaḥanah, He warned Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah for his error of revealing confidential information.
Islam is perfectly just and impartial — each person’s worth before Allah SWT depends solely on their faith and deeds, not on their family ties or social status. We are given three examples of women:
The wives of Prophets Nuh and Lut (PBU Them), who were disbelievers. Despite being married to noble messengers, their relationship did not save them from punishment.
The wife of Pharaoh (Asiyah), who believed in Allah despite her husband’s tyranny and was rewarded with Paradise.
Maryam (Mary), the mother of Isa (Jesus), who was honored with a miraculous birth and chosen as the Leader of the women in Paradise because of her faith, patience, and submission to Allah’ SWTs will.
These examples remind the Prophet’s wives — and all believers — that true honor and salvation come only from personal piety and obedience to Allah SWT, not from association with the righteous.

The Surah affirms that the Prophet (PBUH) received revelation beyond the Quran, known as Wahy (non-Quranic revelation), which guided him in various matters. Ayat 3 of this Surah mentions how Allah SWT informed the Prophet (PBUH) of a private conversation his wife had disclosed. Since this information was not part of the Quran, it clearly proves that Allah SWT communicated with him through other forms of divine inspiration as well.

sections.title: 1-7 DO NOT MAKE SOMETHING UNLAWFUL WHICH ALLAH HAS MADE LAWFUL AND WIVES OF THE HOLY PROPHET ARE ADMONISHED ON THEIR BEHAVIOR WITH HIM

translation.text: O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you? Is it to please your wives? Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Compassionate.

commentary.text: Reason:

The Story of the Honey: The Prophet (PBUH) would visit his wives daily after ‘Asr prayer. He began staying longer with Zaynab bint Jaḥsh because she had been gifted honey, and he enjoyed it. Out of mild jealousy, ʿĀ’ishah, Ḥafṣah, and others conspired playfully to say, whenever he visited, “Your mouth smells of maghāfīr (a resin with an unpleasant odor)” — knowing the Prophet’s refined nature. The Prophet, wishing to avoid any trace of unpleasantness, said:
“I will not drink it again; I have sworn an oath.” Allah SWT then revealed this Ayat to correct him for denying himself something lawful.

This is not a rebuke in the form of a question, but rather an expression of divine disapproval. Its purpose is to make clear that no one—not even the Prophet (PBUH)—has the authority to declare unlawful what Allah SWT has made lawful.

Even though the Prophet’s act was not a legal declaration of prohibition but a personal abstention (done to please his wives), Allah SWT corrected him because as Allah SWT’s Messenger, his personal actions set examples for his followers.
His abstaining from something lawful could have led people to mistakenly believe that it had become religiously undesirable or forbidden.
Allah SWT thus emphasized that legislation belongs to Him alone, and even noble intentions (like harmony within the household) must not lead to altering divine boundaries.
LESSON: DON’T LET SPOUSES HINDER YOUR JOURNEY TOWARD ALLAH SWT. LOVE IN MODERATION.

translation.text: Allah has already ordained for you, (O men), the dissolution of your oaths (in some cases): and Allah is your Protector, and He is Full of Knowledge and Wisdom.

commentary.text: This Ayat clarifies that Allah SWT has provided a way for believers to atone for oaths that prevent them from lawful things. It refers to Surah Al-Mā’idah (5:89), which details how to expiate an oath through feeding or clothing the poor, freeing a slave, or fasting three days. The Prophet (PBUH) was instructed to follow this law when he had vowed to avoid something permissible.
Allah SWT does not punish for a mistaken restriction but provides a wise and fair way to undo it, reinforcing that obedience to divine law outweighs emotional vows or self-imposed prohibitions.

Allah SWT is our Master and Guardian. Human beings are not independent entities in this world; rather we are servants of Allah SWT. Therefore, no one has the authority to alter, amend, or disregard the methods and laws that He has prescribed.

All divine commandments—whether permitting or prohibiting something—are grounded in absolute knowledge and profound wisdom. Therefore, those who truly believe in Allah SWT must acknowledge that it is He who possesses all knowledge and wisdom, not they. Their well-being, both in this world and the next, lies solely in following His guidance and implementing His commands with full faith and obedience.

translation.text: The Prophet confided something to one of his wives and then she disclosed it (to another); so after Allah revealed to the Prophet (that she had disclosed that secret), he made a part of it known to her and passed over a part of it. And when he told her about this (i.e., that she had disclosed the secret entrusted to her), she asked: “Who informed you of this?” He said: “I was told of it by He Who is All-Knowing, All-Aware.”

commentary.text: A delicate incident from the Prophet (PBUH)’s household is being related here, which Allah SWT mentions not to expose personal details, but to teach an enduring moral lesson about trust, confidentiality, and responsibility.

The Prophet (PBUH) confided a matter to one of his wives in private, and she later disclosed it to another. When Allah SWT informed the Prophet of this breach of confidence, he revealed part of what she had said and overlooked the rest out of mercy and discretion. When she asked how he came to know, he replied that it was told to him by Allah, “the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.”

The Quran deliberately leaves the detail unmentioned. This silence itself is instructive. It teaches that the focus is not on the content of the secret but on the act of disclosing it. The ethical principle being that when one is entrusted with confidence—especially in the home of a leader or person of public responsibility—it must be safeguarded completely.

By recording this event in the Quran, Allah SWT intended to train not only the Prophet (PBUH)’s wives but also the wives and families of all those who hold positions of trust and authority within the Muslim community. They are to recognize that their speech and conduct carry consequences beyond their personal sphere.

In sum, this Ayat highlights that confidentiality is a sacred trust. Breaking it, even in seemingly minor matters, can weaken the fabric of trust upon which leadership, faith, and social stability depend. It reminds believers that Allah SWT knows every word uttered and every secret disclosed.

Lesson: Prophet (PBUH) did not talk about the entire incident with Hafsa rather only part of it so as to not make her defensive. Thus, let a person know in a subtle manner so that they can reform themselves. Don’t correct with humiliation and criticism.

translation.text: If the two of you turn in repentance to Allah (that is better for you), for the hearts of both of you have swerved from the Straight Path. But if you support one another against the Prophet, then surely Allah is his Protector; and after that Gabriel and all righteous believers and the angels are all his supporters.

commentary.text: Allah SWT directly addresses ʿĀ’ishah and Ḥafṣah (RA), who had momentarily acted in a way that displeased the Prophet (PBUH). Allah SWT calls upon them to repent, for their hearts had swerved (ṣaghat)—not out of disbelief, but due to human emotion and jealousy that led them away from what was most fitting toward the Messenger of Allah. Their repentance would restore harmony and spiritual balance.

Allah SWT then cautions them: if they continue to support one another against the Prophet, they will gain nothing but harm for themselves. The Prophet (PBUH) does not stand unprotected, for Allah SWT Himself is his Protector, and after Him, Jibrīl, the righteous believers, and all the angels stand by his side.
The Ayat teaches believers the importance of loyalty, restraint, and respect in matters involving the Messenger.

arabic_lines: عَسٰى رَبُّهٗۤ اِنۡ طَلَّقَكُنَّ اَنۡ يُّبۡدِلَهٗۤ اَزۡوَاجًا خَيۡرًا مِّنۡكُنَّ مُسۡلِمٰتٍ مُّؤۡمِنٰتٍ قٰنِتٰتٍ تٰٓـئِبٰتٍ عٰبِدٰتٍ سٰٓـئِحٰتٍ ثَيِّبٰتٍ وَّاَبۡكَارًا

translation.text: Perhaps, if he were to divorce you ˹all˺, his Lord would replace you with better wives who are (i) submissive ˹to Allah˺,(ii) faithful ˹to Him˺, (iii) devout, (iv) repentant, (v) dedicated to worship and (vi) fasting—previously married or virgins.

commentary.text: Reason: This Ayat was revealed at a time when some tensions and rivalries had arisen among the Prophet’s wives. Their natural human emotions — jealousy, hurt, and competition — had led to behavior that caused him distress. In his deep sensitivity and humility, the Prophet (PBUH) withdrew from them for a period, which gave rise to rumors of divorce. In this context, Allah SWT revealed this Ayat to restore order, balance, and reflection within the household of prophethood.

Allah SWT issues a firm yet merciful warning to all the wives of the Prophet (PBUH). After addressing ʿĀ’ishah and Ḥafṣah (RA) in the previous Ayat, the reprimand is now extended to all the noble wives, reminding them of the unique responsibility and dignity of being the spouses of Allah’s Messenger. Allah SWT declares that if the Prophet (PBUH) were to divorce them, He could replace them with wives better than them — women of pure faith, devotion, and character, fully committed to Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH).
Allah SWT describes the qualities of ideal believing women — those who would be worthy of such honor:
Muslimāt (those who submit to Allah) in obedience and humility;
Mu’mināt (those with deep faith) whose belief is both sincere and active;
Qānitāt (obedient) both to Allah SWT and, within what is right, to their husbands;
Tā’ibāt (repentant), constantly turning back to Allah SWT in humility;
ʿĀbidāt (worshipful), devoted in prayer and remembrance;

Sā’iḥāt (fasting or self-restrained), given to spiritual discipline and self-control;
whether they were previously married or virgins.

The Ayat does not deny the existing virtue of the Prophet (PBUH)’s wives but calls them to rise above human frailties and to live in full awareness of the sacred station they occupied as “Mothers of the Believers.” Their conduct was to match the dignity of their home — the very heart of divine guidance. Thus, with Privilege comes with responsibility.
Lesson: Both the terms Muslima and Momin are used.
1. Muslim (مسلم) — One who submits
Derived from “Islam,” which means submission or surrenders to Allah SWT.
A Muslim is someone who outwardly accepts Islam, recites the Shahadah (declaration of faith), performs the pillars of Islam, and lives under the law of Allah.
In other words, being a Muslim refers to external submission — obedience in actions and recognition of Allah and His Messenger (PBUH).
Example: A person who prays, fasts, and follows Islamic practices is a Muslim — even if their inner faith (iman) is still weak or developing.
2. Mu’min (مؤمن) — One who truly believes
Derived from “Iman,” which means deep faith, trust, and conviction in the heart.
A Mu’min not only submits outwardly but also believes inwardly with sincerity and certainty.
Iman is a spiritual state that brings peace, humility, and firm trust in Allah — both in ease and difficulty.
Example: A Mu’min not only performs prayer but does so with full consciousness of Allah (khushu’), trust in His wisdom, and love for Him.
3. Qur’anic Distinction
Allah says: “The Bedouins say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not [yet] believed; but say instead, ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts.” — Surah Al-Ḥujurāt (49:14)
This Ayat shows that Islam (submission) is the first step, while Iman (faith) is a higher level that settles deeply in the heart.

Every Mu’min is a Muslim, but not every Muslim is necessarily a Mu’min.
A Muslim practices Islam outwardly; a Mu’min lives it inwardly and outwardly — with heart, mind, and action united in faith.

translation.text: O believers! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, overseen by formidable and severe angels, who never disobey whatever Allah orders—always doing as commanded.

commentary.text: This Ayat emphasizes that a believer’s duty goes beyond saving himself from Allah SWTs punishment; it extends to guiding and training his family to live in obedience to Allah SWT.
A parent’s true concern should not only be the worldly comfort of their children but, more importantly, their salvation in the Hereafter. Similarly as spouse should not lead you away from your Raab.
The Prophet (PBUH) said, “Each of you is a shepherd and is accountable for his flock,” meaning that leaders, husbands, and wives are all responsible for those under their care.
The angels guarding Hell will carry out Allah SWT’s commands with absolute precision, showing no leniency or deviation in enforcing the punishment decreed for each sinner.
Lesson: Blood relations are being addressed here. Because as we have read earlier spouses and children are our biggest tests and enemies when it comes to obeying Allah SWT.

translation.text: ˹The deniers will then be told,˺ “O disbelievers! Make no excuses this Day! You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”

O believers! Turn to Allah in sincere repentance, so your Lord may absolve you of your sins and admit you into Gardens, under which rivers flow, on the Day Allah will not disgrace the Prophet or the believers with him. Their light will shine ahead of them and on their right. They will say, “Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us. ˹For˺ You are truly Most Capable of everything.”

commentary.text: Allah SWT calls upon the believers to turn to Him in sincere repentance (tawbah nasūh) — repentance that is genuine, humble, and free from hypocrisy. True repentance, as the Prophet (PBUH) explained, means to feel deep regret for one’s sin, seek Allah’s forgiveness with sincerity, and resolve never to repeat the offense. As Sayyidna ʿUmar (RA) said, sincere repentance is when one does not even think of returning to the sin again.
Allah SWT promises that such repentance may lead Him to erase past sins and admit the believer into Gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Lesson: Return from the focus of this world to the focus of the Hereafter. Understand your responsibilities in Islam (see Ayat below). Hell is something that we prepare for ourselves via our actions.

translation.text: O Prophet! Struggle against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be firm with them. Hell will be their home. What an evil destination!

commentary.text: Also see Surah Tuabah Aayt 73.
Prophet (PBUH) nature was gentle, and hypocrites took advantage of this.

translation.text: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. Each was married to one of Our righteous servants yet betrayed them. So their husbands were of no benefit to them against Allah whatsoever. Both were told, “Enter the Fire, along with the others!”

commentary.text: Although these women lived closely with two of Allah SWTs righteous servants, shared their homes, and witnessed their message daily, their proximity did not benefit them because they rejected faith.

According to Ibn ʿAbbās (RA), their betrayal meant refusing to follow their prophets’ religion. The wife of Nūḥ (AS) used to reveal the names of believers to his enemies, and the wife of Lūṭ (AS) informed the sinful people of her town whenever guests came to her husband. Their actions showed disloyalty to truth and support for disbelief.
Thus, Allah SWT declared that their closeness to prophets could not save them. This teaches that faith, not family ties, determines salvation.

translation.text: And Allah sets forth an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh, who prayed, “My Lord! Build me a house in Paradise near You, deliver me from Pharaoh and his ˹evil˺ doing, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”

commentary.text: The wife of Pharaoh, Āsiyah bint Muzāhim, as a shining example of faith and steadfastness. Though she lived in the palace of one of the most arrogant and tyrannical rulers in history, her husband’s disbelief and cruelty did not corrupt her heart or weaken her faith. Allah SWT set her story as a parable for all believers — showing that true faith remains firm even during disbelief and oppression.

Āsiyah secretly believed in Allah SWT after witnessing the miracles of Mūsā (Moses) and declared her faith in “the Lord of Mūsā and Hārūn.” When Pharaoh discovered this, he tortured her severely under the blazing sun, yet her faith never wavered. As she endured the pain, she prayed, “My Lord, build for me a house near You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.” Allah SWT accepted her prayer; her soul was taken gently while she looked upon her home in Paradise.
Just as being close to a prophet cannot save a disbeliever (as seen in the wives of Nūḥ and Lūṭ), being married to a tyrant cannot harm a true believer

commentary.text: Here Maryam (Mary), the daughter of ʿImrān, as another noble example of faith and purity. Allah SWT praises her for guarding her chastity and remaining steadfast despite false accusations. ʿĪsā (Jesus) was miraculously conceived without a father. Her story refutes the false claims made by those who accused her of sin and affirms her complete innocence and virtue.

Maryam believed wholeheartedly in the words and revelations of her Lord and lived with humility and obedience. She represents the model of perfect submission and spiritual devotion — a woman of purity, truth, and steadfast faith. Through her example, Allah SWT shows that true honor lies in faith, chastity, and obedience, not in status or worldly association,

Examples in this surah: the two disbelieving wives of Prophets Nuh and Lut (PBU Them) as warnings although they had ideal circumstances by being married to righteous men, and Asiyah and Maryam as two timeless symbols of righteousness and steadfast belief despite one being in an abusive marriage and one being single.
So the lesson is you are the only one who can lead yourself to success not circumstances.
